purpose:
A single-user macOS dictation application. It captures speech, recognizes it, optionally rewrites it under a user-selected mode, and inserts the result into the application the user was working in. Every speech and language operation runs on the user's Mac. There is no cloud fallback, no account, no subscription gate, and no artificial cap on recording length or usage; the limits are the hardware and the models the user installs.

In scope: recording controls, text delivery, recording display, built-in modes, custom modes, automatic mode selection, vocabulary, context, languages, input sources, meetings, history, models, desktop behavior. Out of scope: cloud inference, account-based settings synchronization, paywalls, enterprise billing and authentication, and any Windows or iOS client.

The whole product is designed before implementation work is cut, because several requirements constrain the persistence schema, the process model and the ingest boundary in ways that are expensive to retrofit: re-recognizing old audio through a different speech model while keeping every derived artifact attributable (D-029), generating meeting notes from a transcript plus a diarization result plus an editable speaker assignment (D-037), deleting a recording while a worker is producing a result for it (D-024, D-033), snapshotting settings so a later edit cannot change the meaning of a saved result (D-006), recovering a crash at any stage without duplicating delivered text (D-010, D-031), and bounding memory on a multi-hour input inside every process that touches it (D-018, D-042). Left to whichever implementation task first encounters them, those force the schema and the job model into a shape that cannot express them.

This revision settles the items the last review found unresolved, and each change is a correction to a contract rather than a narrowing of scope.

Delivery no longer rests on an unevidenced claim about accessibility errors. A settability probe precedes any write, so a target that cannot take selected-text insertion routes to the pasteboard rung without anything having touched it; after a write is issued, fallthrough happens only for error codes in an approved pre-effect class that F4 populates and that ships empty, and messaging failures are never in it (D-009). Delivery profiles carry the application and macOS versions they were measured against and expire, so a stale rejection signal cannot license synthesized typing after an update. The attempt row can no longer rest in a rejected state between rungs, because rejected is a rung outcome and the handoff to the next rung is one transaction (D-010). Submission re-confirms that the delivered text still sits where it was confirmed, not only that the element identity is unchanged.

The no-egress boundary is absolute. The external command-line decoder ships only if F2 shows a spawned child inherits the service sandbox; otherwise the extension mechanism is a decoder implemented inside the sandboxed decode service, and no opt-in transfers trust out of the boundary (D-028, D-018). Model assets a runtime materializes inside its service container are now an owned artifact class with a path, a table, hash verification, lease participation, size accounting and deletion rules, so the storage bound D-038 establishes covers every access mechanism (D-040).

Compatible local model import cannot be blocked by absent provenance. Identity always rests on the installation-manifest hash, publisher and revision fall back to user labels marked provenance unknown, an asset with no recorded notice is importable and only the downloader refuses it, and notices attach to the installation rather than to the shared blob (D-041, D-022).

Long-input behavior is specified and measured for every inference process, not only for recognition. Each model-bound job declares a working-data contract that must be constant in input duration, diarization has a windowed contract with a stated cross-window identity cost, and the long-import protocol samples the decode service and its child as well as the app (D-042, D-023, D-027).

Automatic media resumption now depends on an observable the adapter contract actually supplies: an adapter that can only read current state may pause but never resume automatically, and ownership is revoked by any intervening transition, any stream gap and any state that does not match (D-025). Transformation contract types moved onto the allowed dependency path so the layering rule and the component assignment agree (D-002, D-012).

Where a claim cannot be made, the design says so instead of weakening the feature. Lexical and structural checks on generated text are necessary conditions, not proof of fidelity. Speaker attribution keeps absent evidence as unknown and keeps manual assignment available (D-023). Every measurement that would evaluate a runtime choice is named, given a range with its basis and an action on failure, and marked unperformed.

The historical feature inventories from the mcwhisper and super experiments are evidence about desired scope. Their generated plans and dependency choices do not bind this design.
architecture:
## Layering rule

One rule governs dependency direction. DictationCore depends only on DictationPorts; adapters depend on DictationPorts and on system frameworks; nothing depends on an adapter except the composition root in the app shell. DictationCore contains no AppKit, no AVFoundation, no SQLite and no XPC code, so the run state machine, mode resolution, the vocabulary pipeline, prompt assembly, check disposition, delivery policy and scheduling policy can be exercised without a microphone, a model or a window server.

## Package and target layout (D-002)

A Swift Package Manager package, LocalDictation, with library targets:

- DictationPorts: protocols and value types shared by core and adapters. Ports: AudioSource, AudioFrame, SpeechRecognizer, TextGenerator, Diarizer, DecoderProvider, ContractChecker, TextInserter, FocusObserver, ContextProvider, ModelStore, RecordingStore, LeaseBroker, ShortcutRegistrar, MediaPlayerAdapter, RuntimeCapabilityDescriptor. Value types include TransformationContract, CheckReport, WorkingDataContract, DeliveryProfile and RunManifest, so core can hold a contract and read a report without importing the target that computes it.
- DictationCore: run state machine, RunManifest assembly, mode resolution, vocabulary pipeline, prompt assembly, check disposition, ResourceScheduler policy, delivery policy.
- TextValidation: the ContractChecker implementation, the language-independent check set, and per-language validator packs covering segmentation, interrogative detection and content-word extraction. It is deterministic and pure, and it sits behind the port like any other adapter, which is what removes the earlier conflict between the layering rule and the component assignment.
- DictationStore: SQLite schema, migrations, repositories, the audio chunk journal and its sealer, tombstones, generations, the lease broker, retained-context artifacts, the materialized-asset registry.
- AudioIngest: AVAudioEngine microphone source, ScreenCaptureKit system-audio source, AVAssetReader seekable file source, converters to the canonical recognition format.
- SpeechRuntimeWhisperKit, with SpeechRuntimeWhisperCpp built when Intel coverage is required or when F1 rules the default out (D-020); DiarizerSpeakerKit (D-023); LanguageRuntimeLlamaCpp (D-021). Each publishes a RuntimeCapabilityDescriptor carrying its own revision and its working-data contract.
- InferenceIPC: message types and the connection client shared by the app and the services.
- SystemIntegration: accessibility probing, insertion and readback, pasteboard, CGEventTap shortcuts, player adapters, status item, permission probes.
- DictationUI: SwiftUI views, recording panel, settings, history browser.

Five bundled XPC services. Four carry code that must not reach the network: SpeechService, GenerationService, DiarizationService and DecodeService. The fifth, ModelDownloader, is the only one that may. Each service is a thin main over a library target, so swift test covers its logic. The Xcode app target produces the bundles and owns entitlements, hardened runtime, privacy usage strings and notarization, none of which is expressible in Package.swift.

## Process model (D-003, D-028, D-036, D-040)

The app shell runs unsandboxed, because setting selected text in other applications and running a session-level event tap are unavailable to a sandboxed application outside the Mac App Store; D-036 records the distribution decision that makes this available. Each inference service is sandboxed on its own and its entitlement set omits com.apple.security.network.client, so an outbound connection is denied by the system whatever the linked code contains. That boundary is a constraint of the design and has no fallback outside it.

Model assets reach a service by one of three mechanisms, in preference order: opened file descriptors passed over the connection; a read-only sandbox path exception scoped to Models/blobs for a runtime that insists on opening a model directory by path; materialization by the service of the passed descriptors into a verified cache in its own container, which needs no exception at all and costs a second copy of the assets. F2 decides which mechanism each runtime needs. Materialized caches are not private service state: they are registered, hash-verified, lease-aware, size-accounted and deletable artifacts owned by the store (D-040). If a runtime cannot load under any of the three, it is not used for that model kind and the alternative adapter behind the same port is built; a model kind with no adapter that can load inside the boundary is a product-owner escalation rather than a quiet relaxation of the boundary.

Durable state inside a service is limited to two kinds: the job scratch directory under Scratch/<jobId>, which DecodeService uses for decoded windows and which is removed at job end and swept at launch, and the materialized model cache when F2 selects that mechanism. No service writes prompts, context, audio or transcripts anywhere else, and neither kind holds anything the app cannot rebuild.

The decoder extension follows the same boundary. A user-selected external command-line decoder is offered only if F2 shows that a child of DecodeService inherits the service sandbox, which makes it a shipping condition rather than a setting; if inheritance does not hold, the external adapter is not built and the extension mechanism is a DecoderProvider implementation inside DecodeService, where a format is added by shipping a decoder in the service rather than by pointing at a binary (D-018, D-028).

Diarization has its own service rather than sharing SpeechService. RESEARCH records that this runtime's default initialization may download models, so it is the component whose acquisition control most needs an enforced boundary, and it loads a different model set whose residency and working data are counted separately (D-027, D-042).

Nothing listens on a TCP port. A local HTTP endpoint would bind a port every process on the machine can reach, would need its own authentication, and is the component most likely to acquire forwarding behavior through configuration the app does not own; RESEARCH raises that for llama.cpp's server tooling.

ModelDownloader holds the network entitlement, an allowlist of model hosts, and write access confined to Models/.staging. It runs only on explicit user action, and no inference service can start it.

A service can fail or be terminated independently of its client, so connection interruption is a first-class event. The run fails at its current stage, committed results stand, and the next admission loads the model into a fresh service.

## Processing runs and stages (D-029, D-037)

A recording owns audio artifacts. Every piece of derived text belongs to a processing_run, which pins the settings and inputs that produced it and names its entry stage. Run kinds: dictation (capture through delivery), import, meeting (two-stream capture through diarization), notes, reprocess_recognition, reprocess_diarization, reprocess_text.

The stage set is idle, arming, capturing, sealing, recognizing, diarizing, refining, rewriting, noting, delivering, terminal. A run enters at the stage its kind declares and visits only the stages its kind declares. Every stage a run can occupy has a cancellation effect (D-007) and a recovery transition (D-031).

A notes run is a separate run rather than a tail stage of the meeting run, because its manifest must pin the diarization result and the assignment revision, and those do not exist when a meeting run arms. When a meeting run's diarization result commits, the store also commits assignment revision 1 derived from the clusters, and the app creates a notes run whose manifest names the transcript result, the diarization result, the assignment revision, the identity-name set hash, the mode revision and the generation model installation. Regeneration after a rename, a split or a re-diarization creates another notes run the same way.

## The lifetime of a dictation run (D-006)

Component boundaries follow this sequence.

1. idle.
2. arming. The microphone stream starts immediately on the trigger and its frames go into a pre-roll ring, so the first word is not lost while the rest of arming runs concurrently: resolve the effective mode from the automatic-selection rules (D-014); resolve the delivery target, meaning frontmost process id, bundle identifier, window number, focused accessibility element, that element's readback capability and its selected-text settability (D-008, D-009); sample context sources in parallel against a 200 ms budget and distil them (D-016); assemble a RunManifest naming mode revision, model installations, runtime and adapter revisions, vocabulary revision, language setting, translation flag and validator pack set; allocate a UUIDv7 recording id and run id; create the session directory; write and fsync manifest v0 with disposition active.
3. capturing. The pre-roll ring is flushed into the chunk journal ahead of the live frames (D-030); the writer appends timestamped native frames; the provisional recognizer consumes a parallel tap; the panel shows live text and an envelope (D-011).
4. sealing. Stop the source, drain the sealer backlog, write and commit the finalized artifact (D-030), then commit the recording row, artifact row and run row in one transaction. That is the first point at which the recording exists in History; ownership before it is the session directory (D-033).
5. recognizing. One pass over the complete audio produces a recognition result with segment timings and per-segment average log-probability. The provisional stream is discarded instead of promoted; it was computed over partial context and is a different artifact.
6. refining. Deterministic vocabulary replacement and optional filler removal produce a normalized result derived from that recognition result (D-015).
7. rewriting, only when the mode has a generation stage: prompt assembly, generation in the service, contract checking through the ContractChecker port with disposition decided in core (D-012).
8. delivering. One ladder attempt sequence with per-rung records, guarded by a committed idempotency record (D-010).
9. terminal: complete, cancelled(stage), failed(stage, reason), or delivery_unresolved.

Imports enter at capturing with a seekable source and no delivery target. Meetings enter at arming with two sources, no delivery target, and run through diarizing. Reprocessing enters at recognizing, diarizing, refining or rewriting with a manifest naming its parent inputs. One machine serves every input source and every reprocessing path, which is why cancellation, recovery and deletion each have a single definition.

## Concurrency, lanes and admission (D-004, D-042)

One RunActor per processing run owns that run's state, rows and files, and is the only writer for them. Two runs on the same recording are serialized by the recording's lease (D-033). The audio callback thread never touches an actor, allocates or locks; it writes frames and a 10 ms RMS and peak envelope into two lock-free rings.

A single ResourceScheduler actor admits work of both kinds.

Non-model work is admitted by session count. At most one live capture session runs at a time; a meeting is one session with two streams, and a second trigger while one is active is refused with a message rather than queued. Live capture writing and incremental sealing are exempt from admission and run on a capture lane above batch quality of service, because a live source cannot be deferred without losing data. Seekable ingest is not exempt: an import's decoding, conversion, journaling and sealing occupy one of a bounded number of ingest slots, one by default and configurable to two.

Model-bound work is admitted by slot and by summed footprint, where the footprint of a job is its model residency plus the ceiling of its declared working-data contract (D-027, D-042). Slots are speech-primary, speech-preview, generation and diarization, at most one occupant each. From arming until its recognition result commits, an interactive dictation run holds a reservation on the speech-primary slot: any batch speech job is preempted at admission time, which is why the preview ladder in D-011 always has a rung available rather than waiting behind a long import. Preemption yields and resumes only where the runtime's descriptor records verified checkpoint equivalence; otherwise the batch job restarts from the beginning when it is re-admitted. A user setting can defer preemption until the batch job finishes, at the cost of delaying the dictation, and the panel says which policy is in force.

The sealer has a backlog bound rather than a quality-of-service promise. If the unsealed journal backlog for any live stream exceeds 30 seconds of audio for more than 10 seconds, batch admission pauses; above 60 seconds, ingest slots are released and imports stop; above 120 seconds, capture stops and the recording is sealed as interrupted with the reason recorded. F3 measures the backlog under CPU and disk contention.

## Component responsibilities

- ModeResolver (core): a pure function from foreground application, URL when readable, explicit override and the ordered rule list to a mode revision.
- VocabularyPipeline (core): pure text-to-text with an explicit stage order, an explicit match precedence and ICU-based segmentation.
- ContextDistiller (core): reduces a sampled source to a capped term list, or passes prose when the mode opts in, recording which form was used per source and releasing the raw source at the point D-016 states.
- PromptAssembler (core): mode instructions, then context in the form D-016 allows for its source, fenced with a per-run random delimiter and labeled as reference material, then the normalized transcript, then the task line restated.
- ContractChecker (TextValidation, behind a port): runs the language-independent set always and the language-dependent set when a pack exists, and returns a CheckReport naming which checks ran, which passed and which were unavailable. Disposition is decided in core by D-012.
- DeliveryCoordinator (core policy) with TextInserter (adapter): target resolution, settability probing, revalidation, per-rung fallthrough rules, the confirmation predicate and profile applicability live in policy; only the mechanism lives in the adapter, so the whole ladder is testable without a window server.
- RecordingStore with LeaseBroker (DictationStore): the only writers of History rows, library files, retained-context artifacts and materialized-asset registrations, and the enforcement point for tombstones, generations and leases for every writer including retention.
- InferenceClient (InferenceIPC): connection lifecycle, credit accounting, interruption handling, per-service residency and working-data accounting.

## Why this supports the whole scope as capabilities land

The run state machine, the manifest snapshot, the provenance graph, the recovery table and the lease protocol are built first against fake adapters. Every later capability adds an adapter behind an existing port, a result kind, or a validator language pack. None of them changes how a run is recorded, cancelled, recovered or deleted. The parts that are expensive to change late are exercised against fakes, where cancel-at-every-stage and kill-at-every-boundary suites are cheap to run.
data_lifecycle:
## Stores and ownership

DictationStore owns everything under ~/Library/Application Support/LocalDictation/:

```
library.sqlite                                  metadata, runs, results, FTS index (WAL)
Recordings/<uuid>/manifest.json                 fsynced at run start, carries disposition
Recordings/<uuid>/journal/<stream>/<seq>.pcm    durable capture chunks
Recordings/<uuid>/journal/<stream>/index.log    packet index and seal record
Recordings/<uuid>/audio/<stream>.caf            sealed library artifact
Recordings/<uuid>/source/<original filename>    imported original
Recordings/<uuid>/context/<sampleId>.txt        retained context text, when opted in
Models/blobs/<setHash>/                         immutable verified installs, deduplicated by content
Models/notices/<installationId>/                licences and notices, keyed by installation
Models/.staging/<uuid>/                         in-flight downloads and imports
Scratch/<jobId>/                                service temporaries
```

One further location is owned by the store but lives inside a service container, because a sandboxed service can always write there and needs no exception: ~/Library/Containers/<service bundle id>/Data/Library/Application Support/LocalDictation/materialized/<setHash>/, holding a verified copy of an installation's assets when F2 selects materialization for that runtime, with a materialize.done marker written and fsynced after per-asset hash verification (D-040). The app shell is unsandboxed, so it can enumerate, size and delete those directories; the store, not the service, decides when they exist.

One writer connection in WAL mode; readers use separate connections. RunActor never writes SQLite directly. It calls repository methods that enforce tombstone, generation and lease rules. Notices live outside Models/blobs and are keyed by installation rather than by content hash, so archiving an installation cannot delete the terms it claims to retain, and two installations whose bytes are identical but whose acquisition origin or licence differs keep their own notices while sharing one blob (D-041).

## Ownership before the History row exists (D-033)

A lease requires a recording row, and capture creates that row only at the sealing commit. Between arming and that commit the unit of ownership is the session directory: its path contains a UUIDv7 no other actor can name, the owning RunActor is its only writer, and manifest.json carries a disposition field, fsynced on change, with values active, cancelled and abandoned. Cancellation or deletion requested before the commit is recorded by writing the disposition, not by a tombstone row, and the disposition is durable whether or not the seal has finished. Recovery treats a session directory with no committed recording row according to its manifest disposition. The lease protocol begins at the commit and covers everything afterwards.

## Provenance graph (D-029, D-037)

- recordings(id, created_at, source_kind, duration_ms, interrupted, deleted_at, generation, audio_state, display_run_id)
- audio_artifacts(id, recording_id, role, path, container, codec, sample_rate, channels, sealed_at, sha256, byte_length, rate_reduced), role in {microphone, system, imported_original}
- processing_runs(id, recording_id, recording_generation, kind, entry_stage, manifest_json, runtime_revisions_json, state, started_at, ended_at, reason)
- results(id, run_id, recording_id, kind, primary_input_result_id, text, params_json, params_rendered, created_at), kind in {recognition, normalized, rewritten, translation, diarization, notes}
- result_dependencies(result_id, input_kind, input_id, role), input_kind in {result, speaker_assignment_revision, audio_artifact}, role in {transcript, diarization, assignments, prior_notes, audio}
- segments, derived_segments, speaker_clusters, speaker_identities, speaker_identity_names, speaker_assignment_revisions, speaker_assignments, modes, mode_revisions, vocabulary_revisions, rules, model_installations, model_assets, materialized_assets, active_models, leases, context_digests, retained_context, delivery_attempts, delivery_attempt_rungs, delivery_profiles, jobs

Every result names its primary input through a column, which carries the common single-parent chain: normalized derives from recognition, rewritten from normalized, a translation from whichever result the user translated. Two result kinds have no textual parent and carry NULL there: a recognition result, which roots its run's chain, and a diarization result, whose inputs are audio artifacts. Anything a result depends on that is not its primary input, including entities that are not results, is a row in result_dependencies. A notes result has the transcript as primary input and dependency rows for the diarization result and the assignment revision. The invariants asserted in verification are stated per result kind for exactly this reason.

A recording can hold several recognition results and several diarization results, one per run, each carrying the model installation and the runtime and adapter revisions that produced it. Results are immutable after insert, enforced by a trigger that rejects UPDATE on results.text; reprocessing inserts and never replaces. recordings.display_run_id is a user-movable pointer deciding what the list view shows.

## Speaker assignments, splits and revisions (D-037)

A diarization result is immutable and holds cluster boundaries as segments. Everything the user can edit lives in an append-only revision chain: speaker_assignment_revisions(id, recording_id, diarization_result_id, content_hash, created_at); derived_segments(revision_id, id, source_segment_id, start_ms, end_ms), which is the segment set that revision presents; speaker_assignments(revision_id, derived_segment_id, identity_id, attribution_state). Revision 1 commits with the diarization result and its derived segments are one-to-one with the source segments. Splitting a segment appends a revision whose derived segments subdivide one source segment at a user-chosen boundary; merging speakers and reassigning are revisions over the same structure. Identity display names are append-only in speaker_identity_names(identity_id, name, effective_from), because a rename must not silently change what an older transcript view showed.

A notes run pins the transcript result id, the diarization result id, the assignment revision id and the identity-name set hash in its manifest, and the first three appear in result_dependencies. Note text is immutable, cites derived segment ranges resolved through the pinned revision, and contains the names in effect at generation, so a later rename, split or re-diarization cannot change the note's meaning. History compares the pinned identifiers against current state and shows, on a note, that speakers were renamed, split or re-diarized since it was produced, with a regenerate action that creates a new notes run.

## Persistence choice (D-005)

SQLite through GRDB with FTS5 over result text. History search is a stated requirement and FTS5 with bm25 ranking and snippets is why SQLite wins here; SwiftData and Core Data have no comparable text index and their migration behavior is harder to test against fixtures. Schema versions are numbered migrations, each with a test that runs the migration against a fixture database captured at the prior version. Retained context is not added to the FTS index, so search returns the user's own speech and its derived text rather than the documents that happened to be on screen.

## Audio: journal, sealing, finalization and recovery (D-030)

Capture writes fixed-period chunks, two seconds by default, of raw interleaved Int16 at the source's native rate into journal/<stream>/. Each chunk is written to <seq>.pcm.part, fsynced, renamed to <seq>.pcm, and the directory is fsynced. A chunk carries no header; its format lives in the fsynced manifest, so any complete chunk decodes on its own and a torn final chunk is discardable.

The incremental sealer runs on the capture lane. Its cycle for chunk N is ordered so that the index never names bytes that are not durable:

1. Encode chunk N into ALAC packets.
2. Append the packet bytes to the CAF data chunk in audio/<stream>.caf. The data chunk size field is written as -1 during capture, which CAF defines as extending to end of file, so no header rewrite is needed while recording.
3. fsync the CAF file. Audio bytes are durable before anything refers to them.
4. Append one data record to index.log and fsync it. The record is {magic, kind=data, record_seq, chunk_seq, first_packet_index, packet_count, frames_per_packet, caf_data_byte_offset, caf_data_byte_length, varint packet byte sizes for each of packet_count packets, crc32 over the record}. Per-packet sizes are present because an ALAC packet table cannot be reconstructed from a count and an offset.
5. Delete the journal chunks covered by durable data records, then fsync the journal directory.

Finalization at end of capture is itself crash-safe and repeatable, and its commit point is a record rather than the file's shape:

1. Encode and commit any remaining chunks through the cycle above, so every surviving sample is described by a durable data record before the packet table is written.
2. Append the pakt chunk built from the accepted data records, then fsync.
3. Patch the data chunk size field to its final value, then fsync.
4. Hash the file and append a seal record {magic, kind=seal, last_data_record_seq, pakt_byte_offset, file_length, sha256, crc32}, then fsync.
5. Commit the rows.

Recovery replays index.log from the start, accepting records whose crc32 validates and whose byte ranges lie within the file's actual length; the first record failing either test ends the durable prefix and the rest of the log is discarded, which is how a torn tail is rejected. If the prefix ends in a valid seal record whose file length and hash match the file, the artifact is finalized and recovery stops. Otherwise recovery truncates the CAF file to the end of the last accepted data record, which removes any partially written packet table or size patch, re-encodes and commits any surviving journal chunks through the ordinary cycle, and then runs finalization from step 2. Repeating that sequence after another crash produces the same result, because every step derives from the accepted prefix.

Worst-case loss is the unsealed tail: at most one chunk period plus data the operating system had not yet flushed within it. The exact bound comes from gate F3, which has not been run; the chunk period is the tuning knob if the measurement is worse than expected, and the structural fallback if reconstruction proves invalid at any period is to stop deleting chunks until the finalized artifact has been decoded end to end and hashed, at the cost of journal storage equal to the whole recording.

Canonical recognition format is 16 kHz mono Float32, produced by a converter stage after the ingest port. Sealed dictation audio is 16 kHz mono ALAC at roughly 50 to 60 MB per hour, by arithmetic from 16-bit PCM at 115 MB per hour; meeting streams are sealed at native rate by default, which is larger and is reported in the library size view. If F3's contention measurement forces the encode cost down, the first responses are fewer ingest slots and a higher encode priority; sealing meetings at 16 kHz is a separate user setting rather than an automatic action, because it is an irreversible replacement rather than an additional working copy, and an artifact sealed that way carries rate_reduced so History states that the native-rate audio no longer exists. Lossy encoding is rejected because re-recognition with a better model later is a requirement. Imported files are copied in their original encoding and decoded on demand.

## Model installations, identity, states, notices and materialized copies (D-022, D-038, D-040, D-041)

An installation is identified by a SHA-256 over a content-addressed installation manifest that lists the relative path and SHA-256 of every behavior-affecting asset: weights, tokenizer or vocabulary, model configuration, prompt or chat template, feature-extraction parameters, and any companion file the runtime reads. Hashing only the weight files would let a tokenizer or template change output while History reported the same identity. Publisher and revision are labels beside that hash, not part of it: a download supplies them from the source manifest, and a local import may leave them absent, in which case the installation records provenance_unknown, shows a user-editable label defaulting to Local import plus the first twelve hex digits of the manifest hash, and remains fully usable (D-041).

model_installations records that identity, runtime kind, model kind, declared capabilities, install time, origin, provenance state and lifecycle state in {installed, archived, orphaned_runtime, missing}. model_assets records one row per asset with its own SHA-256, size, licence identifier where known and the path of the retained notice under Models/notices/<installationId>/. An asset with no recorded notice is marked licence unknown, activates normally and is never offered for download.

materialized_assets(installation_id, service_kind, container_path, byte_length, verified_at, state) registers each service-container copy when F2 selects that mechanism. The service copies from passed descriptors, verifies every asset hash against the installation manifest, then writes and fsyncs materialize.done; the app inserts the row only after that marker exists. A directory without the marker, or with a hash mismatch, is removed and re-materialized on next demand. Deletion of a copy happens on model unload after the idle timeout, on archive, on installation deletion, on adapter removal, and at launch for any directory whose setHash has no installed or orphaned_runtime row or has no registered row, and it defers while a lease on that installation is live, under the same protocol as every other artifact. The model manager reports materialized bytes per runtime beside blob bytes, and admission adds them to the storage check at activation.

Every run also records the runtime revision, the adapter revision and the capability-descriptor version in processing_runs.runtime_revisions_json, because two results can share an installation identity and still differ if the runtime changed underneath them.

Archiving is what bounds storage when a runtime is replaced (D-038): the installation row, manifest hashes, capabilities and notices are retained so every History result stays attributable, while blobs and every materialized copy are released. Results also carry params_rendered, a human-readable snapshot of the parameters written at insert time, so an old row remains readable after its adapter is removed from the build.

## Settings snapshots and derived results

A mode is a named entity with an append-only chain of mode_revisions, each content-addressed over prompt, formatting rules, transformation contract, context representation settings, validator language list and model selections. A run's manifest stores revision identifiers. Editing a mode creates a revision and leaves saved results pointing at the revision that produced them, which makes the requirement that later edits must not silently change a saved result structural instead of procedural. History shows the producing revision and diffs it against the current one.

## Context: retention, ownership and ephemeral lifetimes (D-016, D-039)

By default the store keeps a SHA-256 digest, byte length, source kind and representation per context sample in context_digests, and not the text. That is enough to tell a user reprocessing an old recording that the original context is unavailable, without retaining copies of unrelated documents and screens.

When a mode opts into retention, the sample is an owned artifact: retained_context(id, run_id, recording_id, source_kind, representation, path, byte_length, sha256, created_at) with the text in Recordings/<uuid>/context/<sampleId>.txt. The row is written in the same transaction as the run's other rows, the file is fsynced before that commit, and both are removed by the same deletion and retention paths as audio, so retained context cannot outlive its recording. Migrations own the table like any other. Protection is the file system's: the library is not separately encrypted, which is the same posture as the audio and transcripts beside it.

Transient copies have stated release points, and every path is covered rather than only the one that ends in generation. A captured screen frame lives only inside the arming task, is passed to Vision in memory and is released when text extraction returns; it is never written to disk. A source that the mode distils to a term list has its raw string released as soon as distillation returns, which is during arming, so a long capture holds only capped term lists. A source the mode opted into prose holds its string until the earliest of prompt assembly, the end of refining for a run with no generation stage, and the run reaching any terminal state, including cancellation and failure. The assembled prompt lives in the RunActor until the generation reply completes, fails or is cancelled, and in the service in the job arena, freed at job end by the same three paths and destroyed with the process if the service crashes. XPC message buffers are released as credit is returned per window. Generation key-value state is freed at job end or at model unload. Scratch/<jobId> is removed when the job ends and swept at launch.

## Interrupted operations (D-031)

The ordering rule is stated once: an externally visible irreversible effect is preceded by a durable record of intent, which is what delivery does, while a local idempotent effect is followed by its commit, which is what sealing does. Recovery at launch reconciles manifests, files and rows by run state.

- arming: remove the session directory. No rows.
- capturing: seal the journal through the finalization sequence, commit the recording with interrupted set, mark the run cancelled(capturing, crash). Nothing was delivered; History offers recognition.
- sealing: a finalized or partially finalized artifact may exist without rows. Recovery is the idempotent sequence above, after which it commits as for capturing, or applies the manifest disposition if that disposition is cancelled.
- recognizing: no partial transcript is saved; the run becomes failed(recognizing, interrupted); audio is retained; History offers a new recognition run.
- diarizing: no partial diarization is saved, and no partial window results are committed; the run becomes failed(diarizing, interrupted); the recognition result and audio stand; History offers a new diarization run.
- refining: the recognition result is committed and immutable, and refining is a pure function of committed inputs pinned in the manifest, so recovery re-runs it, commits the normalized result and stops.
- rewriting: the run becomes failed(rewriting, interrupted); the normalized result stands; History offers a rewrite run. Recovery never resumes generation.
- noting: the run becomes failed(noting, interrupted); the transcript, diarization result and assignment revision stand; History offers a new notes run.
- meeting completed with no notes run: recovery does not start one, because that would consume a model without user action; History shows notes not generated with a Generate action.
- delivering: any delivery_attempts row in pending, in_progress or unconfirmed becomes needs_review, the run becomes delivery_unresolved, and nothing is re-posted (D-010).
- Scratch directories, staged model directories, unregistered or unmarked materialized directories, and model blobs with no installed or orphaned_runtime row and no live lease are removed. Leases whose holder process is gone are reclaimed (D-033).

## Deletion during active processing (D-024, D-033)

Deletion sets recordings.deleted_at, increments recordings.generation, and signals cancellation to every lease holder. Each worker carries recording id and generation from admission. A worker's commit is one transaction that re-reads the recording row and aborts if the row is missing, tombstoned or at a different generation; on abort it removes its scratch directory and returns. The existence check and the insert cannot be separated, so a late response cannot recreate a deleted recording, and the generation counter covers delete-then-recreate at the same identifier. Deleting a recording that has not yet committed is the pre-commit disposition path.

Hard deletion of rows, artifacts, retained context and FTS entries runs when the last lease on the recording is released, and again at launch. Until then the recording is hidden and reported as deleting instead of as reclaimed space.

## Retention (D-033)

Retention defaults to keeping everything. Optional age-based, size-based and audio-discarding policies are ordinary deletion jobs: they acquire the same leases, observe the same generation checks, and skip any recording with a live lease held by a worker, a player or an export, retrying on the next pass. Discarding audio moves recordings.audio_state to audio_discarded, which History displays; playback, re-recognition and re-diarization are then unavailable while text reprocessing remains available. The first run of any policy lists exactly what it would remove before removing it.

## Cancellation by run stage (D-007)

Cancellation has a defined effect at every stage a run can occupy, and the panel names that effect when it happens. Cancelling one run never alters results committed by another run.

- arming: nothing kept; the pre-roll ring and session directory are discarded; no rows.
- capturing: capture stops; the journal is discarded by default and no History row is created; a per-mode setting seals it as an interrupted recording instead.
- sealing: cancellation returns immediately. It writes the disposition into the fsynced manifest and lets the seal finish in the background, because the seal is idempotent and because a disposition recorded in the manifest is applied whether the seal completes now, later, or only after a crash and recovery. The disposition is by default to remove the artifact and session directory with no row committed, and under the per-mode setting to commit the recording marked interrupted. No later stage is entered. The user never waits on encode or disk, which is what removes the earlier dependence on a backlog figure being a wall-clock bound; if the sealer makes no progress at all, the shed sequence in D-004 has already stopped capture and the manifest still decides the outcome.
- recognizing: the worker stops at its next checkpoint; audio is kept; no partial transcript is saved, because a truncated transcript that looks complete is worse than none.
- diarizing: the worker stops; the recognition result and audio are kept; no partial diarization is saved and no window results are committed, because a segment set covering part of a meeting would be indistinguishable in the transcript view from one covering all of it.
- refining: the recognition result stands; the normalized result is dropped.
- rewriting: generation stops; the normalized result is kept and offered for delivery.
- noting: generation stops; the transcript, diarization result and assignment revision stand; no partial notes are saved.
- delivering: cancellable until the first rung's external effect begins. After that the app records which rung began, reports that delivery was attempted, and stops; it does not try to undo an edit in another application.

## Permissions as a capability matrix (D-032)

Revocation is handled per capability and per run state in place of one global rule. Losing a capability terminates only the work that capability serves.

- Microphone denied at launch: recording controls disabled with a link to the settings pane; file import still works. Revoked during capturing: capture stops, the journal is sealed, the recording is marked interrupted, nothing is delivered.
- Screen Recording denied: system audio and screen context unavailable; microphone recording, all modes, and rules that do not need screen context continue; meetings degrade to microphone only with a visible marker. Revoked during capturing of a meeting: the system stream ends and is marked truncated at a timestamp, the microphone stream continues, and the recording states which streams cover which interval.
- Accessibility denied or revoked: settability probing, selected-text insertion, readback and target revalidation are unavailable, so delivery holds the result rather than posting events into a target it cannot identify; recognition, diarization and rewriting continue to completion.
- Input Monitoring denied or revoked: the event tap cannot run, so push-to-talk is unavailable and toggle falls back to a Carbon hotkey; an in-flight run continues and the panel gains a stop control.
- Automation for a browser denied: URL predicates do not match, rule evaluation continues, and the panel shows that the mode came from the fallback. Automation for a media player denied: that player's adapter is unavailable, so D-025's owned-pause path is unavailable for it and the manual actions remain.
- Restoration: capabilities are re-probed on the relevant system notification and at each arming, and the panel reports a recovered capability once instead of on every session.

## Secure input

If IsSecureEventInputEnabled() is true at arming, the run records but is marked delivery-unavailable up front. If it becomes true by delivery time, the app posts no events, holds the result in History, offers copy, and states that another application has secure input active. Password fields are the common case, and silently dropping text there would be the worst available failure.

## Delivery: target, revalidation, rung rules, profiles and attempt states (D-008, D-009, D-010)

Exactly one delivery target is resolved for each focus outcome:

- The latched element is still focused: the target is the latched element.
- The latched application is frontmost with a different element focused, and the per-mode follow-focus setting is on, which is the default: the target is the currently focused element, resolved at delivery.
- Same application, follow-focus off: no target; hold.
- A different application is frontmost, or the latched application quit: no target; hold, with a card offering Deliver and Copy. Re-activating the latched application first is opt-in, because it steals focus.

Resolving the target once is not enough, because Command-V, synthesized typing and the submit Return reach whatever is focused when each event is posted. The coordinator revalidates immediately before every event-based rung and before the Return: the frontmost process, window number and focused element must still equal the resolved target. Any mismatch ends the attempt as unconfirmed, with no retry, no further rung and no submission.

Confirmation is a predicate over content, not over length. Before the operation the coordinator records the target's selected range and, where readable, its value around the insertion point. After the operation it re-reads and confirms that the expected text appears at the expected insertion location with the caret or selection immediately after it.

Fallthrough is rung-specific, because the rungs differ in what they can prove, and no rung falls through on the absence of an observation.

- Rung 0 is a probe, not an insertion: read whether the resolved element advertises settable selected text, together with its role. If the probe says not settable, or the probe itself errors, no write has been issued and rung 2 follows. This is where most targets that cannot take accessibility insertion are routed, and it needs no claim about what an error after a write implies.
- Rung 1 sets AXSelectedText on the target. AXValue is never set, because RESEARCH records that setting an editable field's value can replace its contents. Once the write is issued, fallthrough is permitted only when the returned error code is in the pre-effect class approved under D-035 and populated by F4 from observed behavior. That class ships empty, so until F4 supplies evidence an error after a write ends the attempt as unconfirmed. A messaging failure or timeout is never admitted to the class, whatever F4 measures, because a request the target was too busy to answer may still be applied. Success without an evaluable predicate is unconfirmed and does not fall through.
- Rung 2 writes the pasteboard and posts Command-V. An unchanged readback is not an explicit negative here: posting the event carries no acknowledgment of consumption, and a delayed consumer can apply the paste after the readback, so treating an unchanged value as rejection is how a paragraph gets typed on top of a paste that later lands. Rung 2 falls through to rung 3 only when an applicable delivery profile records a target-specific rejection signal and that signal fires.
- Rung 3 synthesizes Unicode typing, capped at 400 characters; above the cap the app holds and offers copy.

A delivery profile is applicable only when its recorded bundle identifier, element role, target application version range and macOS version range all cover the running target, and only when its measurement date is within two macOS minor releases of the running system. An inapplicable or expired profile is treated as no profile, which makes rung 3 unreachable for that target and the uncertain outcome unconfirmed. That is what keeps an unmaintained profile from licensing synthesized typing after an application update changes the behavior it was measured against.

Attempt states and transitions (D-010): pending is committed before any event is posted or any accessibility write is issued; in_progress while the ladder is running; delivered on a confirmed predicate; unconfirmed when the predicate is not evaluable, when revalidation fails, or when a rung ends with neither confirmation nor an approved negative, which is terminal for the automatic path; held when no target exists or the cap is exceeded; failed on an error before any effect. Terminal states are delivered, unconfirmed, held, failed and needs_review. Rejection is a rung outcome rather than an attempt state: delivery_attempt_rungs records per rung whether its external effect began, the signal observed and an outcome in {not_started, effect_began, confirmed, rejected, indeterminate}, and writing rung N's rejected outcome together with rung N+1's start is one transaction, so the attempt row is never left in a state that has no recovery transition. At launch, pending, in_progress and unconfirmed become needs_review; delivered, held and failed are left as they are, so a successful past delivery is never re-surfaced. Nothing is ever re-posted automatically.

Pasteboard handling: snapshot before writing, and restore only after a confirmed delivery while changeCount still equals ours, or on the user's explicit Restore clipboard action. There is no timer-based restore, because a delayed consumer can read the pasteboard after any interval the app could pick. After an unconfirmed outcome the transcript stays on the pasteboard and the panel says so. Where the pasteboard cannot be snapshotted, meaning it exceeds the configured snapshot limit or holds promised files or unsupported types, the user is told before anything is written and chooses between proceeding without restore and copy-only.

Submission: the Return is posted after a confirmed delivery, whichever rung achieved it, when the submit modifier was held at stop, and only after a final check that both the target identity and the insertion still hold, meaning the delivered text is still at the location where it was confirmed with the caret or selection immediately after it. A user who moves the caret or edits the field between confirmation and Return leaves the element identity unchanged, so identity alone is not enough to decide that submitting is still what they asked for. A held or unconfirmed attempt never auto-submits.

## Service failures (D-003)

A service crash or termination invalidates the connection. The client marks the run failed at its current stage with the exit status, keeps every committed result, releases the job's credit and slot, and offers retry. Three crashes on one model installation mark it suspect in the model list. Because a service holds only loaded models, the current job's window queue, its prompt and its scratch, retry reloads from the manifest and needs no state salvage. A materialized model cache survives the crash and is reused after its marker and hashes are re-checked. A service that stops consuming credit is treated as hung after a no-progress interval measured against delivered windows, and is terminated by the client.

## Model and runtime failures (D-022, D-038, D-040, D-041)

- Download interrupted or hash mismatch against the installation manifest: the staging directory is removed, no blob is created, the active installation is untouched, and the error names expected and computed digests.
- User-supplied model failing its per-kind load smoke test: it stays in staging with the error attached and nothing is activated. The smoke test checks that the runtime can load the assets and produce output on a fixed sample; it is a capability check and never a quality judgment, so a compatible model with no benchmark row activates normally and is labeled unmeasured.
- User-supplied model with no publisher, revision or notice metadata: activation proceeds. Identity is the manifest hash, the label defaults to Local import plus a hash prefix, provenance is recorded as unknown, assets carry licence unknown, and the only consequence is that the downloader will never offer those assets. Missing metadata is never a compatibility gate.
- Materialization failing, whether by disk space, a hash mismatch or a crash before the marker: the directory is removed, no row is registered, and the job fails at its stage with the space or mismatch named. The active installation and its blobs are untouched, and the next admission retries materialization.
- Model assets missing for a pinned run: if the installation is archived, the run is refused up front with an offer to restore the assets by import or download; if the installation claims installed but assets are gone, the row moves to missing and the same offer appears. Loading never falls back to downloading.
- Runtime or adapter revision no longer present for a reprocess that pinned it: the run is refused with the recorded revision named, and the user can run with the current revision as a new run rather than as a reproduction.
- Pairing exceeding the residency and working-data budget: refused at activation with the arithmetic shown, the refusal stating whether the numbers are measured or declared, and the user can override, because it is their machine.

## Resource and storage failures

- Sealer backlog growth: the shed sequence in D-004 pauses batch admission, then stops import ingest, then stops capture and seals as interrupted, each step reported in the panel with the backlog figure.
- Disk full during capture: capture stops, the journal is sealed to the last complete chunk, the recording is marked interrupted, and the panel reports the reason.
- Journal fsync failing repeatedly: capture stops instead of continuing with an unrecoverable tail.
- Unsupported import format: the source is untouched, the session directory is removed, and the error names the format and, where one exists, the decoder that would cover it (D-018).
- A job exceeding its declared working-data ceiling, observed as service resident size crossing the admitted figure: the job is terminated, the run fails at its stage with the measured figure recorded, and the installation is marked for re-measurement rather than the ceiling being silently raised (D-042).
- Audio device removed mid-run: capture stops and the recording is sealed as interrupted. The app does not silently switch devices under an active recording.
- A second recording trigger while a live capture session is active: refused with a message naming the active session, rather than queued behind it.

## Generated text whose compliance cannot be established (D-012)

Checks are divided by what they need. The language-independent set runs on every generation: expansion ratio against the mode's limit, context overlap rejecting any span of eight or more tokens present in the context block and absent from the transcript, vocabulary term survival, script sanity, and orthographic interrogative-marker detection over the transcript, which finds question marks in the scripts the run uses and cannot find a question asked without one. The language-dependent set needs a validator pack: interrogative survival in order under proper sentence segmentation, content-word recall, and detection of sentences with no content-word support in the input.

An observed violation in either set is a contract violation: the run retries once with a stricter instruction, and on a second violation the delivered text is the normalized transcript, the generated text is retained as a result marked contract_violation, and the panel says which check failed. A sentence with no content-word support is a violation on the same path; for a mode whose contract declares summarization, the citation requirement governs instead and uncited bullets are dropped.

When the run's language has no pack, the language-dependent checks are unavailable rather than failed. The model still runs, and its output is produced, retained, searchable and one click from delivery, because pack coverage must not restrict which models a user may run. What changes is the automatic path: for a mode whose contract declares answersQuestions false, an unavailable question-preservation check means the delivered text is the normalized transcript, whatever the orthographic marker check reports. That check can find a question mark; it cannot establish that no question was asked, so making delivery depend on it would put the protection back on a detector the run does not have. There is no per-mode override, because an override would let a mode declaring that it does not answer questions deliver unchecked rewrites, and the specification's condition is that answering must be explicitly part of the selected mode. A mode intended for a language with no pack can be authored as a revision that declares answersQuestions true, which the mode indicator shows.

Context representation carries its own disposition. All three sources are distilled to a capped term list by default, including focused-element text, which removes instruction-shaped sentences from the prompt rather than detecting them afterwards. A mode may opt into prose per source. When any source contributed prose, automatic delivery of generated text additionally requires the language-dependent set to be available and to pass; otherwise the normalized transcript is delivered and the generated text is held one click away. Prose participation is recorded on the result and shown in the panel and History.

The claim stops there. These checks are necessary conditions. They can pass on text whose meaning changed, and on the prose path an instruction followed in words that do not appear in the context is not detectable by any check listed here. The bounds on the damage are that the transcript is always preserved, that delivery is the only automatic external effect and is reviewable, and that the adversarial corpus in verification is the standing test of how far the checks reach.

## Meeting attribution with weak evidence (D-023)

The diarizer supplies cluster boundaries. RESEARCH establishes that its result type exposes speaker centroid embeddings with cosine-distance helpers, that a speaker may have no centroid, and that the declaration does not establish per-segment confidence or margin outputs. The schema follows that exactly: per-segment calibrated confidence is stored as unknown, no per-segment margin is stored, and the only quantitative evidence retained is centroid cosine distance where a centroid exists. Every segment carries attribution_state in {assigned, unverified, assigned_by_user, unattributed}; without per-segment evidence the default is unverified. The transcript shows the cluster label with an unverified marker, and notes attribute only segments whose state is assigned_by_user or assigned. Where a meeting is diarized in windows (D-042), clusters matched across a window boundary by centroid distance are marked cross-window matched and remain user-confirmable, and clusters that could not be matched appear as separate speakers the user can merge; the transcript states which boundaries were stitched. Cross-recording identity is proposed only where both sides have centroids, is always presented for confirmation rather than applied, and is unavailable for a speaker with no centroid. Segments whose microphone content correlates with delayed system audio are marked probable echo and excluded from microphone-side attribution. A user can assign, merge, split or rename at any time; each edit appends an assignment revision (D-037) and sets attribution_state to assigned_by_user, which no later diarization run overwrites.

## Desktop restore failures (D-025)

Automatic pausing requires a MediaPlayerAdapter that addresses an identified player: the adapter queries that player's state and issues a one-way pause command to it. Automatic resumption requires more, and the adapter contract now says what: an observing adapter exposes a state-change stream as well as a query, and ownership of a pause exists only when the adapter observed the transition from playing to paused on that stream after the app's command. Ownership is revoked by any later transition observed on the stream, by any gap in the stream such as the player quitting or the app restarting, and by any state read that does not match the owned state. A controlling-only adapter, which can read current state but cannot observe transitions, may pause and may offer Resume as a user action, and never resumes automatically, because finding a player paused cannot distinguish an untouched pause from a play and a second pause by the user.

For a player with no adapter the app takes no automatic action. The panel and menu offer Pause media as an explicit user action, which posts the play-pause key and is labeled as a toggle whose recipient and effect the app cannot confirm; the same surface offers Resume playback afterwards. Posting that key automatically is unsafe in a case REVIEW_NOTES names: a paused player can receive the toggle while an unrelated client keeps the output device active, which starts playback. Input device volume is restored only if the current value still equals the value the app set; any mismatch means no restore and a note that the setting was left as found.

## Dependency order among capability areas

- The store, the run state machine, the manifest, the lease protocol and the recovery table depend on nothing external and come first, exercised against fake adapters. Everything else depends on them.
- Capture and delivery depend on the run machine, the recovery contract and the capability matrix (D-006, D-031, D-032). Neither depends on a model, so both can be accepted before any runtime is integrated.
- Recognition depends on capture and on the model store, because a run pins an installation and a runtime revision (D-022), and on the materialized-asset lifecycle when F2 selects that mechanism (D-040).
- Vocabulary and the Standard mode depend on recognition. Generation modes depend on vocabulary, on the check sets and packs behind the ContractChecker port (D-012) and on F2, which governs how the generation service is launched.
- Automatic mode selection and context depend on modes existing, on the retained-context schema (D-039) and on the permission matrix for their degraded states.
- System audio and file import depend on the ingest port, on ingest admission (D-004) and on the memory slopes from F1 and the decode measurement in D-042.
- Meetings depend on system-audio capture, on F5, on the diarization service and its working-data contract, and on the acquisition path for weights the application does not bundle. Notes depend on the notes run and the assignment-revision schema (D-037).
- Languages and retention depend on results and leases already existing; translation is a result kind with its own evaluation set, and retention is a deletion job under the same protocol (D-033).
- Desktop integration depends on capture and delivery only; each player adapter (D-025) is independent of everything else, and the observing adapters are what the automatic path is limited to.

Each area is accepted on evidence approved by the owner named in D-035, against behavior tables written before the tests.

- Store and run machine: the recovery outcome for every non-terminal state, including diarizing and noting, asserted after a kill at that state boundary, matching the approved table.
- Capture: the F3 loss bound within its approved range, a decodable artifact whose packet count matches the durable prefix after every injected kill including kills during finalization and during recovery, and the measured sealer backlog under contention.
- Delivery: the dated F4 matrix with its error-code observations, automated permission-matrix tests, the attempt-state and per-rung tables exercised including equal-length replacement, delayed-consumer paste, a crash between rungs, an expired profile and an edit between confirmation and submission, and a crash-during-delivery test showing needs_review with no re-post.
- Recognition: word error rate rows attached to machine, model revision, quantization and runtime revision, plus the memory slope at three durations measured inside the service.
- Vocabulary: table-driven determinism across match precedence, ordering, boundaries, case and scripts without spaces.
- Modes: human rubric scores on the fidelity corpus including adversarial cases, scored under the rule in verification, plus per-mode violation, checks_partial and prose-hold rates.
- Languages: recognition word error rate per language, and translation adequacy scored on the bilingual set against the retained source transcript, reported separately from mode formatting.
- Models: crash injection between blob rename and the activation transaction, activation while a run holds a lease, an import with no publisher, revision or notice metadata that activates and is labeled unmeasured and provenance unknown, an asset-level change that produces a different installation identity, two installations sharing one blob with different notices, archive and restore with History rows still resolving, materialized-cache creation, reuse, mismatch repair and deletion on unload and archive, and a complete session with the network denied.

## Adding a new input source

A new source implements AudioSource, emitting timestamped native frames plus a SourceDescriptor giving live or seekable, clock domain, known duration, native rate and channel layout, and whether it honors credit. Arming branches on live against seekable, because a live source resolves a delivery target and is exempt from admission while a seekable source takes an ingest slot. The alternative considered was a pipeline per source, each owning its chunking, conversion and cancellation. That is shorter today and duplicates the parts most likely to be wrong: a memory bug on long input would exist only in the import path, and cancellation semantics would drift between paths. The cost of one port is that every source carries timing metadata even when it has one stream and no drift.

## Adding a decoder

The DecoderProvider port takes a source and emits windows under credit. Where F2 shows a spawned child inherits the service sandbox, a user-selected external binary can implement it, and the adapter requires the binary to consume input as a stream and emit windows, so its own memory is bounded and measurable. Where inheritance does not hold, a format is added by building a decoder into DecodeService, which is more work per format and keeps the boundary intact. Either way the decoder is measured in the long-input protocol rather than trusted because its output queue is bounded.

## Replacing a model runtime

Runtimes are separate adapter targets and separate service binaries, each publishing a capability descriptor with measured fields, a revision, a parameter schema and a working-data contract. results.params_json stores parameters under a stable application-level schema with a runtime-specific extension blob, and results.params_rendered stores the human-readable form produced at insert time, so History rows from a removed runtime stay readable after its presentation hook is gone. The settings interface renders common parameters, meaning context length, temperature, beam size, thread count and quantization, generically from that schema, and a runtime may supply presentation hooks for parameters with conditional validity, model-specific ranges or memory effects. Replacing a runtime therefore adds a bounded amount of interface work; a claim that a schema removes bespoke interface work entirely would be too strong.

Storage effect of a swap is bounded by D-038 and D-040 together rather than by garbage collection alone. History results reference their installations permanently, so an installation row is never unreferenced and collection by reference count would retain every superseded model. Archiving separates the two: the row, hashes, capabilities and notices stay, while blobs and every materialized copy are released, and History states that reprocessing through that installation needs them restored. Removing an adapter does not delete anything by itself: its installations move to orphaned_runtime, stay installed, and appear in the model manager with their blob and materialized sizes and an archive action, plus a launch-time notice listing them. Deletion of weights is always a user action.

Calling a runtime API directly from feature code removes a layer. Under that arrangement, swapping runtimes touches every call site, the settings interface and the persisted parameters, and old History rows referencing removed parameter names become uninterpretable. RESEARCH flags long-recording behavior and integration cost as unexamined for both speech candidates, so designing as though the first choice is permanent would be the wrong bet.

## Maintenance costs accepted

- GRDB: a dependency with its own release cadence plus migration discipline, paid for by FTS5 and tested migrations.
- Vendored C and C++ runtimes: long builds, periodic vendoring and upstream API drift. Pinned to tagged revisions with an update checklist that reruns the evaluation harness, refreshes capability descriptors and bumps the recorded runtime revision.
- Accessibility insertion, delivery profiles and the pre-effect error class: per-application behavior is undocumented and changes. The matrix is re-run per macOS minor release and per major update of the applications in it, and both profiles and error-class entries carry the versions they were measured against and expire. An unmaintained entry degrades to unconfirmed outcomes, which is the direction worth paying for.
- Player adapters: one integration per supported player, each with its own automation permission, its own state-change source and its own breakage risk on player updates. A player whose state-change source stops working degrades from observing to controlling-only, which removes automatic resume for it rather than making it unsafe.
- Materialized model caches: a second copy of that runtime's assets per service, a marker and hash-verification path, and sweep rules at launch and on unload. Reported in the model manager so the cost is visible.
- Validator language packs: each language needs segmentation, interrogative detection and a content-word list, plus rubric review in that language. Languages without a pack run the language-independent set and take the disposition in D-012.
- Chunk journal and finalization: extra file management, two fsyncs per chunk period per stream, and a recovery sequence that must stay idempotent.
- XPC services: five bundles to sign, entitlement sets to keep correct, and interruption handling in the client. A missing entitlement fails closed.

## What supporting other Macs would require

Intel support means the whisper.cpp adapter with its own model format, a smaller generation model, its own memory budget and its own evaluation run; RESEARCH notes that documented platform support does not establish comparable performance. Machines with 8 GB need a smaller pairing and a residency policy that unloads the speech model before loading the generation model, at the cost of latency between stages, with diarization sequential to both, the preview slot disabled, and materialization avoided in favor of descriptor passing where a runtime allows it. Both are adapter and policy changes and neither touches the store or the run machine.

## Human review where assertions are weak

Transformation fidelity is reviewed and not only asserted. A fixed corpus of 40 recordings per mode per shipped language has expected outputs, scored against five criteria: meaning preserved, no invented facts, questions still questions, vocabulary terms intact, formatting within the declared contract. Each criterion is scored 0, 1 or 2 against a written definition of each level. Two reviewers score independently, neither being the author of the mode under review; where they differ by more than one point on any criterion a third reviewer adjudicates and that score stands.

The ship rule for a built-in mode revision: no item may score 0 on meaning preserved, no invented facts, or questions still questions, and no more than 10 percent of items may score 1 on any criterion. The structure of that rule is derived from the specification, which forbids inventing content and forbids answering a dictated question outside a mode that declares it; the 10 percent figure and the corpus size are proposals with no empirical basis, and 40 items resolves a violation rate only to roughly plus or minus 9 points at 95 percent confidence, which detects gross failures rather than small differences. A revision that fails is revised and re-scored; a built-in that cannot meet the rule is not shipped as a built-in and the reason is recorded. The corpus includes adversarial cases built to pass lexical checks while changing meaning: removed or inserted negation, swapped quantities, modality changes such as must to may, swapped attribution between two named people, an answer appended after a retained question, a sentence copied from the context block, and an instruction in prose context obeyed in words absent from that context.

Translation is evaluated on its own set, because it is a declared operation rather than one of the built-in modes and because a mode rubric scored in one language cannot say whether an English translation preserved a Spanish sentence. For each source language with a shipped recognition default, a bilingual set of 30 utterances has reference English translations written by a fluent speaker of both languages. Scoring compares the English result against the retained source transcript, not against the audio, so a recognition error is attributed to recognition rather than to translation, and the recognition word error rate for the same items is reported beside it. Two bilingual reviewers score adequacy, names and numbers preserved, and no added content, each 0, 1 or 2 with the same adjudication rule. Ship rule for the default pairing in that language: no item scores 0 on adequacy or on names and numbers, and no more than 10 percent score 1 on any criterion; the figures carry the same basis note as the mode rubric. chrF is reported alongside as a descriptive number and gates nothing, because a surface metric cannot distinguish a paraphrase from a meaning change.

Meeting notes are scored on the mode scale with citation validity checked automatically and the uncited-bullet drop rate tracked; a note whose bullets cite segments that do not support them scores 0 on no invented facts.

Basis: structural, since the two capture paths exist and channel origin is certain, while echo from speakers into the microphone is not accounted for by structure alone. Reconsider after diarization and echo evaluation; if a mixed-stream diarizer performs comparably, the second stream becomes an optimization.

The diarizer supplies cluster boundaries and centroid embeddings with cosine-distance helpers, supplies no per-segment confidence or margin, and may supply no centroid for a given speaker. Basis: stated in RESEARCH for SpeakerKit v1.1.0's DiarizationResult declaration, from source inspection with no inference experiment run. The schema therefore stores per-segment calibrated confidence as unknown, stores no per-segment margin, and uses centroid distance only for identity proposals the user confirms. Reconsider at F5, which inventories the fields actually exposed at the pinned version.

Whether the diarizer holds memory proportional to input duration is unknown, and the windowed contract in D-042 needs no capability the SDK is not already known to have. Basis: RESEARCH says nothing about long-recording behavior for this component, and a window-and-stitch arrangement uses only whole-input diarization on a bounded window plus the centroid comparison the API exposes. Reconsider at F5's duration measurement; if whole-input operation measures flat within its ceiling it is used, and otherwise windowing applies with its cross-window identity cost measured rather than assumed away.

Lossless 16 kHz mono audio at roughly 50 to 60 MB per hour makes indefinite dictation retention acceptable by default, while native-rate meeting streams are large enough to surface in the library size view. Basis: arithmetic from 16-bit PCM at 115 MB per hour and typical lossless ratios. Reconsider when a library crosses a user-visible size threshold, at which point the retention interface is surfaced instead of a default quietly applied.

A 200 ms arming budget is tolerable for mode resolution, target resolution, settability probing and context sampling, and context sources missing it are skipped for that run. Basis: a design choice about perceived responsiveness with no user study; audio capture does not wait on it because the pre-roll ring starts at the trigger, so the budget affects context completeness rather than lost speech. Reconsider if screen-context sampling routinely misses the deadline and users want it, which moves sampling off the arming path and makes the rewrite stage wait for it.

The pasteboard snapshot limit of 10 MB is a starting value, not a measured threshold. Basis: chosen to avoid duplicating large images and file promises in memory during a latency-sensitive operation, with no measurement of snapshot cost. It is a configurable setting, and F4 records snapshot time by content type so the default can be set from data. Reconsider once that measurement exists.
