The language-detection acceptance threshold starts at 0.5 on the probability the runtime reports. Basis: a proposal with no measurement, chosen so that a detection the runtime does not favor over all alternatives falls back to the mode default rather than steering a transcript. Reconsider from the detection measurement in verification, which reports accuracy at the threshold and the share of confident misdetections.

Retained context text, captured audio and transcripts are protected by file-system permissions and whatever full-disk encryption the user has enabled, not by application-level encryption. Basis: consistency with the rest of the library, which has the same exposure, and the absence of a stated threat model that separates context from audio. Reconsider if a threat model asks for at-rest encryption, which would apply to the library as a whole rather than to context alone.

Weights the application offers for download are limited to assets whose notices permit redistribution, and everything else is user-imported. Basis: RESEARCH records the WhisperKit model card as MIT and records component-specific notices for the diarization collection referring to WeSpeaker and VBx. Reconsider per asset as the notice inventory is compiled; an asset that cannot be offered stays importable with its licence recorded as unknown, so no feature depends on the outcome.

decisions.title: macOS baseline and hardware target
decisions.choice: Deployment target macOS 14.0 and Apple Silicon for the first release, with later-OS APIs gated at runtime and never required.
decisions.rationale: The speech runtime selected in D-020 and the diarizer in D-023 ship in one Swift package whose prerequisites RESEARCH records as macOS 14 and Xcode 16, so the floor follows a dependency the design has committed to. ScreenCaptureKit system-audio capture is available at 14; the WWDC24 microphone stream output arrived later, and microphone capture uses AVAudioEngine on every supported version, so the newer output is off the critical path. Apple Silicon only in the first release is an engineering decision, not a reading of the specification: a second architecture requires its own model format, its own memory budget and its own evaluation run, and doing that before the primary target has any measurement spends effort on a comparison neither side of which is known.

alternatives.option: Baseline macOS 15 for the unified ScreenCaptureKit microphone and system-audio stream
alternatives.tradeoff: One capture path and a shared clock for meetings, at the cost of excluding Sonoma users for a convenience the two-stream design handles with host-time alignment and tone-derived drift correction.

alternatives.option: Baseline macOS 13
alternatives.tradeoff: Wider reach; falls below the selected package's stated prerequisite and adds an operating system to the support matrix that nothing is evaluated on.

alternatives.option: Ship Intel and Apple Silicon together
alternatives.tradeoff: Broader hardware coverage; doubles the evaluation burden that RESEARCH warns documentation cannot substitute for, and forces a second model tier before the primary target is measured.

decisions.consequences: Meetings align two streams by host time instead of receiving them from one, and the alignment range in verification is what decides whether that holds. Intel users wait for the second speech adapter and its own evaluation, and the reason is recorded here rather than attributed to the specification. Any API newer than 14 sits behind an availability check with a defined fallback.
decisions.reconsider_when: The Argmax dependency is dropped, measured two-stream drift exceeds its range after correction, or an Intel requirement is confirmed.

decisions.title: Package layout and dependency direction
decisions.choice: One SPM package with a pure core, a ports target holding protocols and the value types they exchange, a deterministic validation target behind a ContractChecker port, adapter targets per external concern, service targets for inference, and a thin Xcode app shell as the composition root. Core depends only on ports; nothing depends on an adapter except the shell. TransformationContract, CheckReport, WorkingDataContract, DeliveryProfile and RunManifest live in DictationPorts.
decisions.rationale: The scope includes a speech runtime that may be replaced, four input sources, a diarizer, and an insertion mechanism whose behavior varies per target application. Each is an adapter. Keeping the run state machine, mode resolution, the vocabulary pipeline, delivery policy and check disposition free of system frameworks is what lets the earliest work exercise cancel, crash, delete-during-processing, delivery ladders and retention races before any runtime or window server is involved. The previous revision left the transformation contract and the checker in the validation target while core decided their disposition, which no permitted dependency edge supported; putting the value types and the checker protocol in ports makes the layering rule and the component assignment agree without giving core a second dependency. Service logic living in library targets keeps it inside swift test even though the bundles are produced by Xcode.

alternatives.option: Let core depend directly on TextValidation
alternatives.tradeoff: One fewer protocol, and the target is deterministic so it would not break testability; core then imports a concrete implementation, which makes swapping check strategies or stubbing an unavailable pack a code change in core rather than a wiring change.

alternatives.option: Single application target with feature folders
alternatives.tradeoff: Faster early progress; every behavioral test then needs permissions and real models, and swapping a runtime touches feature code throughout.

alternatives.option: Separate SPM packages per subsystem in a workspace
alternatives.tradeoff: Stronger boundaries and independent versioning, at the cost of cross-package version churn for a single application with one consumer.

decisions.consequences: Adapters need explicit wiring in the shell and value types at the boundary in place of framework types passed around. DictationPorts carries more than protocols, so it must stay free of behavior beyond value semantics, which is a review rule. The application bundle cannot come from swift build alone, so there are two entry points: swift test for logic and the Xcode scheme for the shipping application and its signed services.
decisions.reconsider_when: The port boundary starts needing per-adapter escape hatches that leak framework types into core, which would mean the abstraction is fighting the domain.

decisions.title: Inference runs in bundled sandboxed XPC services, one per model kind, with three model-access mechanisms
decisions.choice: Speech recognition, generation, diarization and decoding each run in a bundled XPC service, sandboxed on its own with com.apple.security.network.client withheld. Model assets reach a service by opened file descriptors, by a read-only path exception scoped to Models/blobs, or by materialization into a verified cache in the service's own container, whichever F2 shows the runtime needs. Materialized caches are store-owned artifacts under D-040, not private service state. Durable service-local state is limited to the job scratch directory and that cache. No inference runs in the app process and nothing listens on a port. There is no unsandboxed inference service.
decisions.rationale: RESEARCH's follow-up records that bundled services have separate sandboxes, that a service can fail or be terminated independently of its client, and that signed services with network entitlements withheld are the thing to evaluate for inference; it also states that a scan for socket symbols cannot establish that a process lacks network access. A withheld entitlement is a property of the process, so it covers linked frameworks and dynamically loaded code that a scan cannot reach. Three access mechanisms are named because a failed access method must not become a reason to leave the boundary; the third needs no exception at all, so loading failure is a runtime-selection problem. Naming the two durable service-local artifact kinds removes the earlier contradiction between offering materialization and asserting that a service writes nothing to disk. Diarization gets its own service because RESEARCH records that its runtime's default initialization may download models, and because it loads a different model set whose residency and working data are counted separately.

alternatives.option: Fall back to an unsandboxed service when sandboxed loading fails
alternatives.tradeoff: Guarantees some runtime can always be used; replaces system-enforced egress denial with a symbol scan that RESEARCH rejects as evidence.

alternatives.option: Child helper processes over an inherited socket pair
alternatives.tradeoff: Full control of launch and lifecycle with no launchd involvement; provides no system-level egress denial.

alternatives.option: Link the runtimes into the application process
alternatives.tradeoff: Lowest latency and no serialization boundary; a native crash kills the app mid-run and address-space growth from model loading persists for the process lifetime.

alternatives.option: Run diarization inside SpeechService
alternatives.tradeoff: One fewer bundle to sign; couples two model sets in one residency slot and gives the runtime with documented implicit-download behavior the same process as the one without it.

alternatives.option: Run the upstream HTTP server on localhost
alternatives.tradeoff: Reuses upstream tooling; opens a port every local process can reach and turns the offline property into a claim about configuration the app does not own.

decisions.consequences: Connection interruption is a normal event: the run fails at its stage, committed results stand, and the next admission rebuilds the service. Audio windows cross the connection under credit, so the memory ceiling is measured in each service as well as the app. If F2 selects materialization for a runtime, that runtime's assets exist twice on disk, registered and swept under D-040 and reported in the model manager. Five bundles are signed with their own entitlement sets, and a missing entitlement fails closed.
decisions.reconsider_when: F2 shows a runtime cannot load under any of the three mechanisms, which selects the alternative adapter behind the same port rather than relaxing the boundary.

decisions.title: Concurrency, lanes, admission of non-model work, and interactive slot reservation
decisions.choice: One actor per processing run owning its state and rows; a real-time audio callback writing into lock-free rings; a single ResourceScheduler actor with a capture lane, an interactive lane and a batch lane. Live capture writing and incremental sealing are exempt from admission and run above batch quality of service, bounded instead by one concurrent live capture session. Seekable ingest is admitted: an import's decoding, conversion, journaling and sealing occupy one of a bounded number of ingest slots, one by default. Model slots are speech-primary, speech-preview, generation and diarization, at most one occupant each, with admission checking the summed model residency plus declared working-data ceilings against D-027. An interactive dictation run reserves the speech-primary slot from arming until its recognition result commits, preempting batch speech work. Preemption resumes from a checkpoint only where the runtime descriptor records verified equivalence; otherwise the batch job restarts whole. The sealer has a backlog bound of 30 seconds of audio per live stream with a shedding sequence: pause batch admission, then stop ingest, then stop capture and seal as interrupted.
decisions.rationale: The scope puts a latency-sensitive dictation path beside long batch work on a machine that cannot hold several models resident, so admission belongs in one testable place. Only live sources lose data when deferred, which is the line the exemption follows. Reserving the speech-primary slot for interactive runs is what makes the preview ladder in D-011 executable rather than nominal. A quality-of-service level is not a guarantee, so the sealer gets a numeric backlog bound and a shedding sequence.

alternatives.option: Exempt all capture-stage work from admission
alternatives.tradeoff: One rule for a stage; unbounded concurrent imports each hold windows, journals and buffers outside any budget.

alternatives.option: Admit live capture like any other work
alternatives.tradeoff: Uniform accounting; a queued live capture loses audio that cannot be recovered.

alternatives.option: Serial queue, first come first served
alternatives.tradeoff: Predictable; the user waits behind a batch job, which is the failure the requirements care about most.

alternatives.option: Leave batch speech work running and let the preview wait
alternatives.tradeoff: Imports finish sooner; the recording display has no provisional text during exactly the runs that need it.

alternatives.option: Concurrent residency of every model kind with no admission control
alternatives.tradeoff: Better pipelining on a large machine; on the 16 GB target it invites swap.

decisions.consequences: A long import is interrupted whenever the user dictates, and restarts whole unless its descriptor allows resume; a setting lets the user prefer the import, at the cost of delaying the dictation. A second recording trigger during a live session is refused rather than queued. The audio callback thread has hard constraints that need review discipline.
decisions.reconsider_when: Descriptors show a runtime whose resume reproduces the unpreempted transcript, allowing cheaper preemption, or measurements show a machine class where concurrent residency fits and the single-slot rule costs latency for nothing.

decisions.title: Persistence: SQLite with FTS5 for metadata and text, files for audio and retained context
decisions.choice: SQLite through GRDB in WAL mode for metadata, runs, results, leases and result text, with FTS5 over result text; audio and retained context text in per-recording directories. Numbered migrations with fixture-based migration tests.
decisions.rationale: History requires search across transcripts and results, and FTS5 with bm25 ranking and snippets is the reason to prefer SQLite. Deletion during active work, lease acquisition and model activation all need a transaction that combines a check with a write. Keeping large text and audio out of the database keeps backup, integrity check and migration times short, and keeps retained context out of the search index so results are about the user's own speech.

alternatives.option: SwiftData
alternatives.tradeoff: Least code for models and views with native observation; no full-text index, and migration behavior is harder to test against fixtures for a schema that must survive many capability additions.

alternatives.option: Core Data with an external search index
alternatives.tradeoff: Mature and Apple-supported; adds a second index to keep consistent with deletions, which is the consistency problem the tombstone and lease rules exist to contain.

alternatives.option: Raw libsqlite3 with a hand-written wrapper
alternatives.tradeoff: No third-party dependency; reimplements migrations, statement caching and observation.

alternatives.option: JSON files per recording with an in-memory index
alternatives.tradeoff: Inspectable and easy to back up; search, leases and transactional deletion become bespoke, and the index is rebuilt every launch.

decisions.consequences: A dependency with its own release cadence and migration discipline. FTS triggers must stay in sync with result inserts and deletes, covered by tests. Database and files can disagree after a crash, which the recovery contract resolves.
decisions.reconsider_when: The system SQLite lacks FTS5 on the baseline, in which case GRDB is built against a bundled SQLite, or library sizes make a per-recording file layout with an external index preferable.

decisions.title: Processing runs as explicit state machines with a per-run settings snapshot
decisions.choice: A state machine per processing run over the stages idle, arming, capturing, sealing, recognizing, diarizing, refining, rewriting, noting, delivering and terminal, in the pure core, with a RunManifest written and fsynced at run start pinning mode revision, model installation ids, runtime and adapter revisions, vocabulary revision, language setting, translation flag, validator pack set and, for reprocessing and notes, the parent inputs. A run visits only the stages its kind declares. Run kinds are dictation, import, meeting, notes, reprocess_recognition, reprocess_diarization and reprocess_text. Microphone capture starts at the trigger into a pre-roll ring, so arming work runs concurrently with capture.
decisions.rationale: The manifest is what makes settings snapshots real: a run reads its manifest and never live settings, so editing a mode or switching models mid-run cannot change what a result means. Notes are a separate run kind because a manifest is fsynced at run start and the diarization result and assignment revision do not exist then. Attaching the machine to a run instead of to a recording is what lets one recording carry several recognitions and several diarizations without ambiguity. Starting capture at the trigger removes the case where a push-to-talk user speaks during arming and loses the first word.

alternatives.option: Read live settings at each stage
alternatives.tradeoff: No snapshot machinery; a mode edit during a long recognition silently changes the result's meaning.

alternatives.option: One meeting run through noting with a manifest extension committed before noting
alternatives.tradeoff: One run per meeting and a simpler list; the manifest stops being a single fsynced snapshot and recovery has to reason about which extension was durable.

alternatives.option: Implicit state through nullable columns
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer types; illegal states become representable and per-stage cancellation loses its single definition point.

alternatives.option: One state machine per recording
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler list view; a second recognition has nowhere to live and reprocessing has to mutate the recording's state.

decisions.consequences: A meeting produces at least two runs, which the detail view groups. If the app crashes between a meeting's diarization commit and the creation of its notes run, recovery does not start generation; History shows notes not generated with a Generate action. Settings changes take effect on the next run. The pre-roll ring holds audio before any mode decision, so cancellation during arming discards it explicitly.
decisions.reconsider_when: A requirement needs mid-run settings changes, such as switching language during a long meeting, which would need a segmented manifest in place of one per run.

decisions.title: Cancellation contract defined for every stage a run can occupy
decisions.choice: A stage-indexed table of cancellation effects enforced in core and shown in the panel, covering arming, capturing, sealing, recognizing, diarizing, refining, rewriting, noting and delivering, as listed under failure behavior. Cancellation during sealing returns immediately, records the disposition in the fsynced manifest and lets the idempotent seal finish in the background or at recovery. Cancelling a reprocess or notes run leaves every earlier run's results intact.
decisions.rationale: The specification requires defined effects at every processing stage. Four judgment calls carry the table: sealing does not block the user, because the disposition is durable and the seal is idempotent whether it completes now or after a crash, which removes the earlier dependence on a backlog figure that bounds audio rather than wall-clock time; recognizing saves no partial transcript because a truncated transcript that looks complete is more damaging than an absent one; diarizing saves nothing partial for the same reason applied to segment coverage; rewriting keeps the normalized result because the expensive work is done and the user usually still wants their words.

alternatives.option: Block cancellation until the seal completes
alternatives.tradeoff: The outcome is applied before the user looks away; a stalled disk makes the escape path unresponsive for an unbounded time.

alternatives.option: Abort sealing immediately and delete
alternatives.tradeoff: Stops sooner; leaves a partially finalized artifact whose recovery needs special cases that idempotent completion avoids, and discards audio the user may have asked to keep under the per-mode setting.

alternatives.option: Cancel always discards everything
alternatives.tradeoff: One rule; throws away a completed recognition because the user did not want the rewrite.

alternatives.option: Prompt at cancel time
alternatives.tradeoff: No wrong default; a modal on the escape path is when a user least wants a dialog.

decisions.consequences: Workers need checkpoints so cancel is prompt without being abrupt. A cancelled recording can disappear from the panel before its files are gone, so the panel says finishing when the seal is still running. The panel needs a per-stage message so the effect is visible when it happens.
decisions.reconsider_when: Usage shows repeated re-recording after cancels during recognition, which would argue for keeping partial transcripts clearly marked as partial.

decisions.title: Delivery target resolved once per focus outcome and revalidated before every posted event
decisions.choice: At arming, latch the frontmost process id, bundle identifier, window number, focused accessibility element, that element's readback capability and its selected-text settability. At delivery the target is resolved once: the latched element when it is still focused; the currently focused element when the latched application is frontmost with a different element focused and the per-mode follow-focus setting is on, which is the default; no target, meaning hold, when follow-focus is off, when another application is frontmost, or when the latched application quit. Immediately before each event-based rung and before the submit Return, the coordinator revalidates that the frontmost process, window number and focused element still equal the resolved target; a mismatch ends the attempt as unconfirmed with no retry and no submission. Re-focusing the latched target is opt-in. Only dictation runs deliver.
decisions.rationale: The intended target is the one the user was looking at when they started speaking, and the panel is non-activating (D-011) so showing it does not disturb the latch. Resolving one target per outcome removes the contradiction between policy and mechanism. Resolution alone is not enough, because Command-V, synthesized typing and Return reach whatever is focused when each event is posted, and processing can take seconds. Holding instead of inserting into an unexpected application is conservative because text placed in the wrong window can be unrecoverable and can be sensitive, while a hold costs one click.

alternatives.option: Resolve once and post without revalidation
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer accessibility round trips; a focus change between rungs sends text or a Return into an unrelated window.

alternatives.option: Always deliver into whatever is frontmost at delivery time
alternatives.tradeoff: No held results; text lands in the wrong application whenever focus changes during processing.

alternatives.option: Always act on the latched element regardless of focus
alternatives.tradeoff: One target for every case; writes into a field the user has left.

alternatives.option: Always hold and require confirmation
alternatives.tradeoff: Never wrong; adds a click to every dictation, which defeats the tool.

decisions.consequences: The panel needs a held state with actions and History must show undelivered results. Revalidation adds an accessibility query before each posted event, which is cheap compared with the insertion itself. The same-application default will occasionally insert into a different field in the same window, which matches clicking into the target field while speaking and is a per-mode setting for users who disagree.
decisions.reconsider_when: Holds fire often enough to annoy, which would argue for making opt-in re-focus the default for users who enable it.

decisions.title: Insertion ladder with a settability probe, an evidence-based pre-effect error class, versioned profiles and a content-based confirmation predicate
decisions.choice: Rung 0 probes whether the resolved element advertises settable selected text; a negative or failed probe issues no write and routes to rung 2. Rung 1 sets AXSelectedText; AXValue is never set. After a write is issued, fallthrough is permitted only for error codes in an approved pre-effect class that F4 populates from observed behavior and that ships empty, and messaging failures and timeouts are excluded from that class permanently. Rung 2 writes the pasteboard and posts Command-V; an unchanged readback is not an explicit negative, and rung 2 falls through to rung 3 only when an applicable delivery profile records a target-specific rejection signal and that signal fires. A profile is applicable only when its bundle identifier, element role, target application version range and macOS version range cover the running target and its measurement is within two macOS minor releases; otherwise it is treated as absent. Rung 3 synthesizes Unicode typing capped at 400 characters. Every rung is confirmed by one predicate: the expected text at the expected insertion location with the caret or selection immediately after it. Any outcome that is neither a confirmation nor an approved negative is unconfirmed, which stops the ladder. The pasteboard is restored only after a confirmed delivery while the change count is ours, or on the user's explicit action.
decisions.rationale: RESEARCH distinguishes an accessibility object's value from its selected text and notes that setting an editable field's value can replace its contents, so insertion is a selection-aware operation. It also states that posting a paste event supplies no acknowledgment that the target consumed the clipboard, and REVIEW_NOTES records the delayed-consumer case. The previous revision treated any non-success accessibility error as proof that nothing happened, which nothing in the cited material establishes: a busy or unresponsive target can return a messaging failure after queuing the write, and falling through then inserts twice. The probe carries the case that error classification was really being used for, namely a target that cannot take selected-text insertion, and it does so before anything is written. What remains uncertain stays unconfirmed until F4 supplies per-code evidence. Versioning profiles closes the matching hole on the paste rung, where a rejection signal measured against one application version could otherwise license typing after an update changed the behavior.

alternatives.option: Treat any non-success accessibility error as pre-effect
alternatives.tradeoff: Reaches rung 2 more often with no measurement; duplicates text whenever the error was a messaging failure over a write the target later applied.

alternatives.option: Unchanged readable value counts as rejection
alternatives.tradeoff: Reaches more targets automatically; duplicates text whenever a consumer applies the paste after the readback.

alternatives.option: Stop after rung 2 in all cases
alternatives.tradeoff: Never types; loses the one path that works in targets with no accessibility insertion and a rejecting paste handler.

alternatives.option: Profiles without version scoping
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler table and broader coverage; a signal measured on an old version can fire spuriously after an update, which is the case where typing on top of a paste happens.

alternatives.option: A dedicated input method
alternatives.tradeoff: The system-supported route for inserting text; requires the user to install and select an input method, changing their typing setup for a dictation feature.

decisions.consequences: Rung 3 is unreachable for any target without an applicable profile, so synthesized typing is rare and the common uncertain outcome is unconfirmed with the transcript on the pasteboard. Until F4 populates the pre-effect class, a rung-1 error after a write always ends the attempt, which costs a click in targets where the probe was optimistic. Profiles and class entries are shipped data with dated version scope and an expiry, which is a standing maintenance obligation.
decisions.reconsider_when: F4 supplies per-code evidence that admits an error class, finds targets that expose a genuine rejection signal, or a supported API for inserting text into another application appears.

decisions.title: Delivery idempotency, an attempt-state table with no non-terminal resting state, and no automatic retry
decisions.choice: Commit a delivery_attempts row naming recording, result, run, target and state before any event is posted or any accessibility write is issued, and a delivery_attempt_rungs row per rung recording whether its external effect began, the signal observed and a rung outcome in {not_started, effect_began, confirmed, rejected, indeterminate}. Attempt states are pending, in_progress, delivered, unconfirmed, held, failed and needs_review; rejection is a rung outcome and never an attempt state, and writing a rung's rejected outcome together with the next rung's start is one transaction, so the attempt row never rests anywhere without a recovery transition. Terminal states are delivered, unconfirmed, held, failed and needs_review. On launch, pending, in_progress and unconfirmed become needs_review; delivered, held and failed are untouched. The app never re-posts automatically.
decisions.rationale: A paste into a target that cannot be read back gives no confirmation, so after a crash the app cannot distinguish delivered from about to deliver, and any automatic retry risks inserting the same paragraph twice. Committing before acting means recovery always sees an attempt was in flight. Per-rung records exist because the ladder can begin an external effect on one rung and stop on another. Moving rejection out of the attempt states closes the earlier gap where a crash between rungs left a row in a state the launch rule did not name, and doing the handoff in one transaction means no crash window exists between the two writes.

alternatives.option: Keep rejected as an attempt state and add a recovery transition for it
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer schema changes; the state means the ladder is mid-flight, which is what in_progress already means, so two states would describe one situation.

alternatives.option: Retry pending deliveries on launch
alternatives.tradeoff: Recovers a crash before posting; duplicates text after posting, with no way to tell the cases apart.

alternatives.option: No attempt record, recover from run state
alternatives.tradeoff: One fewer table; the window between deciding to deliver and acting is exactly where a crash is unrecoverable without a durable record.

alternatives.option: One attempt row with no rung detail
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler schema; a needs_review item cannot say which mechanism touched the target.

decisions.consequences: After a crash mid-delivery the user gets a needs_review item naming the last rung whose effect began, and decides. Re-delivery is always explicit. The state and rung tables are part of the approved behavior tables and are asserted transition by transition, including a kill between rungs.
decisions.reconsider_when: A target class emerges whose consumption can be acknowledged, which would make a bounded automatic retry safe for those targets specifically.

decisions.title: Recording display as a non-activating panel, with a preview ladder that always produces text
decisions.choice: An NSPanel with nonactivating and borderless style, status-bar level, joining all spaces, movable by background, ordered front without becoming key. Provisional text renders in a secondary style with a live label; the final transcript replaces it in the primary style with a brief change highlight. The waveform is drawn from a 10 ms RMS and peak envelope computed allocation-free on the capture thread. Failures appear as a row with a short reason and one action. Placement is stored as a fraction of the display's visible frame plus the display identifier, clamped to the primary display when either is gone. Interactive runs reserve the speech-primary slot (D-004), and the preview ladder is: the primary model's streaming pass; a preview-class model under 400 MB in the speech-preview slot; batched updates at voice-activity pauses. Each rung must show first text within 1.5 s of speech onset, update at least every 2 s, drop no capture frames and be non-inferior on final word error rate under the paired test in verification. Waveform-only is not an accepted end state.
decisions.rationale: The panel must never become key, since activating it would break the delivery target that D-008 depends on. Provisional and final text are different artifacts, so they are shown differently and the provisional stream is never persisted. Fractional placement survives resolution and display changes. A provisional live transcript is a named requirement, so the ladder is written to always have a rung: reserving the slot for interactive runs and giving the preview model its own capped slot is what makes that true rather than nominal. If no rung meets its criteria on the evaluation target, that is a release question for the product owner rather than a silent scope reduction.

alternatives.option: A normal SwiftUI window
alternatives.tradeoff: Standard behavior and less AppKit; it activates the application and changes the frontmost application, breaking delivery targeting.

alternatives.option: Menu bar popover only
alternatives.tradeoff: No extra window; anchored to the menu bar so it cannot sit near where the user is typing.

alternatives.option: Degrade to waveform and a voice-activity indicator
alternatives.tradeoff: Guarantees capture is never disturbed; drops a named requirement.

alternatives.option: Promote the provisional transcript as the final result
alternatives.tradeoff: Feels faster; delivers text produced from partial context as final.

decisions.consequences: A preview-class model is a second small installation to manage and to count in the budget, and the panel labels which rung is active. Panel focus and level behavior is AppKit-managed with SwiftUI content and needs its own tests. Users see text change when the final transcript arrives, which is highlighted rather than silent.
decisions.reconsider_when: Measurement shows the primary pass costs dropped buffers or fails the non-inferiority bound, which selects a lower rung rather than removing the preview.

decisions.title: Modes as versioned revisions with structured contracts, split check sets, and a stated disposition for every unchecked path
decisions.choice: Every mode carries a structured TransformationContract, a value type in DictationPorts, holding allowed operations, an answersQuestions flag, a content bound expressed as a recall threshold or a citation requirement, the languages its validator supports, and per-source context representation, alongside its free-form prompt. Revisions are content-addressed and runs pin a revision id. Checking runs through the ContractChecker port and returns a CheckReport naming which checks ran; disposition is decided in core. The language-independent set always runs: expansion ratio, context overlap rejecting spans of eight or more tokens present in context and absent from the transcript, vocabulary survival, script sanity, and orthographic interrogative-marker detection reported as a signal. The language-dependent set needs a pack: interrogative survival in order, content-word recall, unsupported-sentence detection. An observed violation retries once with a stricter instruction and then delivers the normalized transcript, retaining the generated text marked contract_violation. Without a pack, the generated text is still produced, retained and one click from delivery, but for a mode declaring answersQuestions false the delivered text is the normalized transcript, with no override. Context is distilled to a capped term list per source by default; prose is per-mode opt-in per source, and when any prose context is present automatic delivery additionally requires the language-dependent set to be available and to pass.
decisions.rationale: Prompt wording cannot enforce that a dictated question stays a question, so permitted transformations are a machine-checkable property with a defined failure path. The disposition does not depend on the orthographic marker, because a marker can show that a question exists and cannot show that none was asked. There is no override, because one would let a mode declaring that it does not answer questions deliver unchecked rewrites, and the specification requires answering to be explicitly part of the selected mode. Distilling every source, including focused-element text, removes an unchecked instruction path rather than detecting it afterwards. Putting the contract and report types in ports is what lets core own disposition without importing the checker.

alternatives.option: Prompt instructions only, no checks
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplest; the failure mode is a model answering a dictated question and the answer being pasted into a document.

alternatives.option: Keep a per-mode override for unpacked languages
alternatives.tradeoff: No degradation for multilingual users; lets a mode contradict its own declaration.

alternatives.option: Skip generation entirely when no pack exists
alternatives.tradeoff: Uniform conservatism; makes pack coverage a restriction on model use, which is unrelated to the requirement.

alternatives.option: Pass focused-element context as prose unconditionally
alternatives.tradeoff: Better rewrites of a draft in the field; leaves an untransformed instruction path with only after-the-fact detection.

alternatives.option: Validate with a second model asked whether the output is faithful
alternatives.tradeoff: Catches semantic drift lexical checks miss; costs a second generation pass on the latency path and inherits the same failure mode.

decisions.consequences: Modes cannot be saved without a contract, which the editor makes quick with presets. Term-list context is less useful to a model than prose, so modes that need prose opt in and accept a hold when checks are unavailable. Rewriting in a language with no pack is produced and retained but not delivered automatically for modes declaring answersQuestions false, and the panel says why with a one-click deliver. Thresholds need tuning against the fidelity corpus, and bad thresholds show up as frequent visible fallbacks.
decisions.reconsider_when: Violation and hold rates stay high on correct outputs, the adversarial corpus finds a violation class that passes every check, or term-list context proves too lossy for the modes that most need context.

decisions.title: Built-in mode set and their contracts
decisions.choice: Four read-only built-in modes, each with an explicit contract. Standard: punctuation, capitalization, optional disfluency removal, vocabulary substitution; no reordering, no summarizing, no answering. Email: Standard plus salutation and sign-off from a template, paragraph breaks, register adjustment, no new factual content, recall-bounded body. Note: adds list and heading structure, recall-bounded. Meeting notes: summarization permitted, bounded by a citation requirement where every bullet references a real derived segment range and uncited bullets are dropped. All four declare answersQuestions false and default every context source to term-list form. English packs ship first; other languages take the disposition in D-012.
decisions.rationale: The specification asks for ordinary dictation plus task-specific output with permitted transformations specified per mode. Meeting notes is the one mode where summarization is the point, so recall cannot be its guard and a citation requirement fits what it is allowed to do.

alternatives.option: One configurable mode with toggles
alternatives.tradeoff: Less to explain; the contract dissolves into a toggle matrix that is hard to check against.

alternatives.option: A larger built-in catalog
alternatives.tradeoff: More coverage out of the box; each mode needs its own fidelity corpus and rubric, and custom modes already cover these.

alternatives.option: Ship an assistant mode that answers dictated questions
alternatives.tradeoff: An obvious use of a local language model; it is the behavior the requirements single out as a hazard, so it would declare answersQuestions and be visibly distinct in the mode indicator.

decisions.consequences: Built-ins are read-only; customizing one duplicates it into a user mode carrying the same contract as a starting point, which keeps the built-in fidelity corpus meaningful. Four modes means four rubric corpora per shipped language, scored under the rule in verification. Translation is evaluated on its own bilingual set rather than through these corpora, because it is a declared operation rather than a mode.
decisions.reconsider_when: Users routinely duplicate a built-in to make the same edit, which is evidence the built-in should change.

decisions.title: Automatic mode selection: ordered rules, list order as the whole precedence rule, latched at arming
decisions.choice: An ordered rule list evaluated at arming, first match wins, ordered by the user. List position is the complete precedence rule; there is no priority field and no runtime specificity comparison. The editor proposes an insertion position by specificity (URL host plus path prefix, then host, then bundle identifier, then any) and flags rules that can never fire because an earlier rule shadows them. The selected mode is latched into the run manifest. A predicate whose input cannot be obtained does not match, and evaluation continues; if nothing matches, the user's default mode applies.
decisions.rationale: First match on a user-ordered list is the model people know from mail filters and makes conflict resolution inspectable by reading the list top to bottom. Specificity stays in the editor as a suggestion at authoring time, so runtime behavior never depends on a comparison the user cannot see. Treating an unobtainable predicate as a non-match keeps a missing permission from producing a wrong mode. Latching at arming means the mode cannot change under the user mid-sentence.

alternatives.option: Highest specificity wins regardless of order
alternatives.tradeoff: No shadowed rules; the user cannot temporarily override a specific rule with a general one, and precedence stops being visible.

alternatives.option: An explicit numeric priority field with specificity as tiebreak
alternatives.tradeoff: Fine-grained control; two ordering mechanisms to reconcile and a list whose display order does not determine behavior.

alternatives.option: Re-evaluate continuously during capture
alternatives.tradeoff: Follows the user across windows; the mode could change mid-sentence and the run would no longer have one manifest.

alternatives.option: Infer the mode from what was said
alternatives.tradeoff: No rules to configure; requires recognition before mode selection, inverting the pipeline.

decisions.consequences: The effective mode and whether it came from a rule or the fallback appear in the panel and menu bar for every run. Users reorder rules by dragging, which is the only precedence control. Switching applications mid-recording keeps the mode chosen where the user started. Browser URL availability is enumerated per browser instead of assumed.
decisions.reconsider_when: Rule lists grow long enough that manual ordering is unmanageable, which would argue for grouping rather than a hidden precedence rule.

decisions.title: Vocabulary as staged passes with a defined order and an explicit match precedence
decisions.choice: Four stages in fixed order. Recognition biasing puts selected terms in the decoder prompt slot, capped to the runtime limit, chosen by mode relevance and recency. Deterministic replacement scans the recognition result left to right; at each position it considers every rule matching there, takes the longest match, and breaks ties among equal-length matches by list order, applying replacements once with no cascading, boundary-aware using ICU word segmentation for the run's language, case-preserving and non-overlapping. Filler removal is a separate per-mode pass. After generation the replacement table is applied once more and vocabulary survival is checked. Recognition and normalized results are both retained. For scripts without word spacing, replacement uses ICU segmentation where available and otherwise falls back to substring matching with a warning in the vocabulary editor.
decisions.rationale: The mechanisms fail differently and must not be conflated. Prompt biasing changes decoding probabilities and guarantees nothing, so the interface says so. Deterministic replacement is exact and belongs on text. The post-generation pass exists because a language model will sometimes normalize an unusual proper noun back to a common word. Stating longest match with list order as the tie-break removes ambiguity under which two implementations could produce different normalized transcripts while satisfying the same prose.

alternatives.option: Pure list order, first matching rule wins
alternatives.tradeoff: Easy to explain; a short rule earlier in the list pre-empts a longer, more specific one.

alternatives.option: Replacement only after generation
alternatives.tradeoff: One pass; the generation stage then reasons over text containing mis-recognized terms.

alternatives.option: Ask the language model to apply the vocabulary
alternatives.tradeoff: Handles inflection that literal matching misses; makes an exact user-specified substitution probabilistic.

alternatives.option: Cascading replacement to a fixpoint
alternatives.tradeoff: Handles chained rules; introduces order-dependent results and possible loops.

decisions.consequences: Two texts per run to store and show. The editor must explain that terms have one probabilistic effect and one exact effect, and must show which rule won when two overlap. The prompt slot forces selection when the vocabulary is large, so the panel can show which terms were included.
decisions.reconsider_when: A runtime exposes real biasing or constrained decoding, which moves exact-name handling into recognition.

decisions.title: Context sources: sampled at arming, distilled by default, digest-only retention, stated ephemeral lifetimes on every path
decisions.choice: Three optional sources sampled in parallel at arming against a 200 ms deadline: focused-element text, selection and window title through accessibility, capped at 4000 characters; one frame of the focused window through ScreenCaptureKit with Vision text recognition, opt-in; the first text item on the pasteboard, capped. Every source is distilled to a capped term list before it reaches the prompt unless the mode opts that source into prose, and prose carries the disposition in D-012. Anything missing the deadline is omitted and recorded as omitted. Retention defaults to digest, length, source kind and representation; retaining text is opt-in per mode and stored as an owned artifact (D-039). Release points are stated for every path: the screen frame dies when Vision returns and is never written to disk; a distilled source releases its raw string when distillation returns, during arming; a prose source releases at the earliest of prompt assembly, the end of refining for a run with no generation stage, and any terminal state including cancellation and failure; the assembled prompt lives in the RunActor and in the service job arena until the generation completes, fails or is cancelled; XPC buffers are released per credit window; generation key-value state is freed at job end.
decisions.rationale: Sampling once at arming bounds cost and makes a run reproducible; continuous sampling would make the same recording produce different prompts depending on timing. Digest-only retention keeps the library from accumulating copies of unrelated documents and screens while letting a reprocess report that the original context is gone. The previous release rule keyed on prompt assembly, which never happens for a run with no generation stage, so a long capture under such a mode could hold raw context for hours; keying on the earliest of assembly, the end of refining and any terminal state covers every path a run can take.

alternatives.option: Sample at generation time
alternatives.tradeoff: Fresher context and screen recognition off the latency path; by then the user has often switched windows.

alternatives.option: Retain full context text by default
alternatives.tradeoff: Reprocessing reproduces the original result exactly; the library accumulates screen and clipboard contents by default.

alternatives.option: Continuous screen sampling during capture
alternatives.tradeoff: Captures what changed while speaking; sustained recognition cost and a much larger retention question.

decisions.consequences: Screen recognition may routinely miss the deadline on busy displays and is then absent and noted. Reprocessing a recording whose context was not retained produces a different result, and History shows why. The term-list default means context contributes vocabulary and names rather than sentences unless a mode opts in, which reduces its usefulness for drafting modes and is the price of removing an unchecked instruction path.
decisions.reconsider_when: Term-list context proves too lossy for the modes that most need context, which would argue for a structured intermediate representation rather than raw prose.

decisions.title: Languages: per-mode selection or detection with a recorded threshold, translation as a derived result of a named parent
decisions.choice: Each mode sets recognition language to an explicit code or to auto. Auto uses the runtime's language identification; at or above a threshold that starts at 0.5 the detected language is used, and below it the run records undetermined, uses the mode's default language, and the panel says so. Translation to English is a separate declared operation producing a result whose primary input names the exact recognition or normalized result it translated, and it is evaluated on its own bilingual set rather than through a mode rubric. Each model installation declares supported languages, labeled in the interface as declared by the publisher and unmeasured until an evaluation row exists.
decisions.rationale: Recognition quality, rewriting quality and translation adequacy are different properties measured by different methods, so they are represented and evaluated separately; scoring a translation against the retained source transcript is what keeps a recognition error from being charged to translation. Naming the parent result is what makes translation provenance survive a second recognition of the same audio. The detection threshold is written down with a starting value and a measurement rather than left to the first implementation, because its effect is a transcript in the wrong language when it is too low and an unnecessary fallback when it is too high.

alternatives.option: Always auto-detect
alternatives.tradeoff: Nothing to configure; short utterances and code-switching produce wrong detections and the user cannot pin a language they know.

alternatives.option: Leave the detection threshold to implementation
alternatives.tradeoff: One fewer number to approve; the value decides how often a confident wrong language reaches a transcript, which is a product behavior rather than a tuning detail.

alternatives.option: Translate by replacing the transcript
alternatives.tradeoff: One text per recording; the original wording is unrecoverable, breaking reprocessing and review.

alternatives.option: Translate as part of the rewrite
alternatives.tradeoff: One pass; translation and formatting become entangled and a failed check cannot separate a translation error from a formatting one.

decisions.consequences: History shows several artifacts per recording and must make the parent of each obvious. A user-supplied model with an inaccurate manifest can overstate coverage, so the interface attributes the claim to the manifest. Rewriting in a language with no validator pack is produced and retained but not delivered automatically for modes declaring answersQuestions false (D-012). Every shipped source language needs a bilingual evaluation set as well as a recognition set.
decisions.reconsider_when: Measured detection accuracy makes a different threshold or an auto default defensible, or a runtime provides per-segment language identification supporting code-switching.

decisions.title: One ingest port carrying timing and flow control, with a declared format matrix and an in-boundary extension mechanism
decisions.choice: All sources implement AudioSource, emitting AudioFrame values carrying stream id, clock domain, presentation time, sequence number, discontinuity flag, native sample rate, channel layout and sample format. Conversion to the canonical 16 kHz mono Float32 recognition input is an explicit stage after the port. Consumers grant credit; a seekable source stops decoding when credit is exhausted, and a live source that overruns drops frames and records a discontinuity instead of buffering without bound. Credit extends across the service connection. Microphone via AVAudioEngine, system audio via ScreenCaptureKit, files via AVAssetReader in 30-second windows. Initial matrix: wav, aiff, caf, mp3, m4a in AAC and ALAC, mp4, m4v, mov. Extension is a DecoderProvider port with two possible implementations, chosen by F2: a user-selected external command-line decoder run as a child of DecodeService, offered only if that child is confined by the service sandbox, or a decoder built into DecodeService. Either implementation consumes its input as a stream and emits windows under credit, and both are measured in the long-input protocol.
decisions.rationale: An untimestamped canonical buffer cannot express what meetings need, which is two native streams aligned by host time with drift and gaps visible, and it cannot express backpressure. Windowed decoding bounds the decoder; credit bounds the queues between decoder, converter and recognizer, including across the connection. RESEARCH notes whisper.cpp's example has input-format constraints, so an explicit decoding boundary is needed regardless of which runtime ships. The extension mechanism is stated as two implementations rather than one with a disclosed exception, because the specification asks for an extension mechanism and also requires that captured audio stay on the Mac; a decoder inside the service satisfies both when inheritance does not hold.

alternatives.option: Keep the external decoder available with a disclosed trust transfer when inheritance fails
alternatives.tradeoff: Every format the user can find a binary for works; an opt-in cannot waive a requirement that the user's audio stays on the machine, and the process handling it would be unconstrained.

alternatives.option: Canonical untimestamped buffers
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplest consumer code; meeting alignment and gap reporting have to travel around the abstraction, and flow control has nowhere to live.

alternatives.option: Decode whole files into memory
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplest of all; a three-hour file at 16 kHz Float32 is roughly 700 MB before any model loads.

alternatives.option: Bundle a general-purpose decoder
alternatives.tradeoff: Every format works out of the box; adds licensing obligations, binary size and a security update duty for a decoder parsing untrusted files.

decisions.consequences: Every source carries timing metadata even when it has one stream and no drift. Live overrun is a visible discontinuity rather than a silent gap. If F2 rules out the external adapter, adding a format is a code change in DecodeService rather than a user action, which is slower and is the cost of keeping the boundary absolute. Canonical conversion discards content above 8 kHz for recognition, so imported originals are kept and meeting streams are sealed at native rate by default.
decisions.reconsider_when: A speech runtime benefits from a higher input rate, or a supported system decoder covers the formats that drive the extension mechanism.

decisions.title: Imports are copy-in and commit-late, leaving the source untouched
decisions.choice: Import opens the source read-only, copies it into the session directory, and records a security-scoped bookmark for provenance. The recording row commits only when the artifact is complete and readable. On any failure the session directory is removed and no row exists. Moving the original happens only after commit, as a step the user can decline.
decisions.rationale: A failed import leaves its source unchanged if the import path never opens the source for writing and never deletes it. Committing after the artifact is complete keeps a failure from leaving a History entry pointing at nothing.

alternatives.option: Reference the source in place
alternatives.tradeoff: No duplication; the library breaks when the user moves or deletes the file, and reprocessing later finds nothing.

alternatives.option: Transcode on import and discard the original
alternatives.tradeoff: Smaller library and one decode path; discards information and makes reprocessing with a better decoder impossible.

alternatives.option: Create the row first and fill it in
alternatives.tradeoff: Progress visible immediately; a failure leaves a broken row for recovery to reason about.

decisions.consequences: Imports duplicate storage, visible in the library size view and covered by retention. Large video imports copy the whole file though only the audio track is used; extracting only the audio is a refinement once the cost is measured.
decisions.reconsider_when: Large video imports become common enough that storing extracted audio plus a bookmark beats keeping the original.

decisions.title: Speech runtime: WhisperKit ships, whisper.cpp is the F1 comparison harness and the designed second adapter
decisions.choice: Ship WhisperKit from the Argmax Swift package behind SpeechRecognizer, loaded inside the sandboxed speech service with an explicit local model folder and acquisition disabled. Build a measurement-only whisper.cpp harness as part of F1, not as a shipping adapter, so the retention comparison is executable, with the comparator checkpoint and quantization rule fixed and approved before the gate runs. Promote it to a full adapter when Intel coverage is required, when F1 misses a range, or when the notice inventory rules the first choice out.
decisions.rationale: Three pieces of evidence in RESEARCH support choosing now instead of deferring: the runtime is distributed as a Swift package and the stated build is SPM, so integration cost is lower than a C API that also needs its own decoding boundary; the WhisperKit model repository states MIT on its card, the only positive licensing evidence available for weights the application might offer for download; and SpeakerKit ships in the same package, so the diarizer that Meetings requires arrives through one dependency. What RESEARCH does not establish is accuracy, latency or long-recording behavior. Building the comparison arm as measurement code inside F1 removes the circularity of a retention rule that depended on an adapter to be built only after retention failed, and fixing the comparator in advance keeps it from being chosen after results are visible.

alternatives.option: whisper.cpp as the shipping runtime
alternatives.tradeoff: Intel and Apple Silicon coverage today with widely available GGML weights; C interop in the hot path, an explicit decoding boundary its example demands, and a second dependency and acquisition path for diarization.

alternatives.option: Maintain both runtimes permanently
alternatives.tradeoff: Maximum flexibility; two parameter translations, two evaluation runs per model update and two descriptor sets, paid before any evidence says both have a role.

alternatives.option: An absolute word error rate threshold instead of a comparison
alternatives.tradeoff: No second arm to build; an absolute number for a mixed-language corpus has no defensible basis and would be invented.

alternatives.option: Apple's built-in speech recognition
alternatives.tradeoff: No models to manage; on-device availability and language coverage are controlled by the system and model choice is not exposed, which the requirements demand.

decisions.consequences: F1 carries the cost of a second measurement path. Intel is unsupported until the harness is promoted. Results record the installation, runtime revision and adapter revision, so a change is visible in History. Until F1 completes, no accuracy or latency claim appears anywhere.
decisions.reconsider_when: F1 misses any of its approved ranges, the notice inventory blocks the weights the app would offer, or Intel becomes a requirement.

decisions.title: Generation runtime: llama.cpp embedded in the generation service, GGUF models
decisions.choice: Embed llama.cpp as a library in GenerationService, loading GGUF models with Metal on Apple Silicon and CPU otherwise, streaming tokens back over the connection. No server binary is used or shipped. The adapter publishes a working-data contract covering key-value cache and workspace as a function of context length rather than of input duration.
decisions.rationale: RESEARCH records llama.cpp as providing local inference with Metal support and as shipping both library integration material and server tooling, and asks that an embedded worker be compared with a local service including whether network access is possible. Embedding gives control over acquisition and lifecycle, and GGUF reaches the quantized models users already have, which matters because user-supplied models are in scope. Generation working data scales with context, not with recording length, which is why a long meeting is handled by windowed notes rather than by a larger context.

alternatives.option: MLX-based generation
alternatives.tradeoff: Apple-native with good Apple Silicon performance; a different model format, fewer ready quantizations and no Intel path.

alternatives.option: Core ML converted models
alternatives.tradeoff: System-managed execution and no vendored C++; per-model conversion work, and user-supplied models become impractical.

alternatives.option: The llama.cpp server on localhost
alternatives.tradeoff: Reuses upstream tooling; the reachability and forwarding concerns in D-003 apply directly.

decisions.consequences: Vendored C++ with build time, pinning and update discipline, and a runtime revision recorded on every run. Quantization and context length become user-visible settings with memory consequences surfaced through D-027.
decisions.reconsider_when: MLX coverage of the quantizations users bring becomes comparable, or measured generation latency is unacceptable and another runtime measurably beats it.

decisions.title: Model identity over every behavior-affecting asset, immutable installs, transactional activation, per-kind checks, notices keyed by installation
decisions.choice: Identity is a SHA-256 over a content-addressed installation manifest listing the relative path and SHA-256 of every behavior-affecting asset: weights, tokenizer or vocabulary, model configuration, prompt or chat template, feature-extraction parameters and companions. Publisher and revision are recorded labels beside that hash and may be absent for a local import (D-041). Installation stages into Models/.staging/<uuid>, verifies per-asset and manifest hashes, runs the smoke test for its model kind in the matching service against the staged path, then renames into Models/blobs/<setHash>, a path never previously written. One SQLite transaction inserts the installation row, its per-asset rows and the active pointer; notices are written under Models/notices/<installationId>/, keyed by installation rather than by content so two installations sharing a blob can carry different terms. Every run records the runtime revision, adapter revision and capability-descriptor version. Per-kind compatibility and smoke tests: speech needs encoder, decoder and tokenizer and transcribes a three-second fixture; generation needs weights with a tokenizer and produces 16 tokens from a fixed prompt and seed; diarization needs segmenter, embedder and clusterer and returns at least one segment on a ten-second two-speaker fixture. Quality scores never gate activation. Runtimes receive absolute paths and never load by name.
decisions.rationale: A sequence spanning a filesystem rename and a database update needs an ordering rule, and renaming over a live directory is not atomic. Hashing only the weight files would let a tokenizer, template or configuration change output while History reported the same identity, and a runtime update would do the same invisibly, so identity covers every asset the runtime reads and the run pins the code revision beside it. Keying notices by installation rather than by content hash was the fix for a conflation the earlier layout created: identical bytes acquired from different origins can carry different terms, and the blob is shared while the terms are not. A single generic smoke test cannot catch a diarizer missing its clusterer, so the descriptor and the test are per kind. RESEARCH warns that a default runtime initialization may download models, so passing explicit paths is the enforcement point.

alternatives.option: Notices under the blob hash
alternatives.tradeoff: One directory per unique content; two installations of the same bytes under different terms cannot both be represented, and archiving the blob would take the notices with it.

alternatives.option: Hash the weight files only
alternatives.tradeoff: Cheaper on multi-gigabyte installs; two installs identical in weights but differing in tokenizer or template are indistinguishable in History.

alternatives.option: Install in place and roll back on failure
alternatives.tradeoff: No staging space needed; a failure during the write leaves a corrupt live model.

alternatives.option: One generic load test for every model kind
alternatives.tradeoff: Less per-kind work; misses missing companion assets, which then fail mid-dictation.

alternatives.option: Let the runtime's own downloader manage models
alternatives.tradeoff: Much less code; hands acquisition to a component that may download implicitly.

decisions.consequences: Installation needs free space for the staged and stored copy, and for a materialized copy where F2 selects it, checked before starting. Hashing large files is shown as a verification step. A runtime update changes the recorded revision on new runs, so History can distinguish results the same installation produced under different code. Blobs can outlive their rows briefly after a crash and are collected at launch.
decisions.reconsider_when: Hashing time becomes a usability problem, which argues for incremental hashing during download, or a new model kind arrives whose descriptor does not fit the per-kind pattern.

decisions.title: Meetings: SpeakerKit diarization in its own service under a bounded working-data contract, channel origin as fact, attribution as hypothesis
decisions.choice: Record microphone and system audio as separate artifacts with role recorded as a capture fact, aligned by host time with tone-derived drift correction. Diarize with SpeakerKit's Pyannote pipeline behind a Diarizer port in DiarizationService, configured with download disabled, an explicit model folder and explicit segmenter and embedder concurrency, all recorded in the manifest. The adapter honors the working-data contract in D-042: it uses whole-input operation only if F5 measures its peak resident size flat in duration within the stated ceiling, and otherwise runs bounded analysis windows of 10 minutes with 30-second overlap, committing segment rows per window and matching clusters across boundaries by centroid distance, with stitched boundaries marked and unmatched clusters left separate for the user to merge. Weights are user-acquired and never bundled. Diarization is a run stage with cancellation, recovery and admission. Per-segment calibrated confidence is stored as unknown and no per-segment margin is stored. Centroid cosine distance, where a centroid exists, proposes cross-recording identity for user confirmation and never applies one. Segments correlating with delayed system audio are marked probable echo. Notes are generated by a separate notes run over the timestamped transcript in overlapping windows with per-bullet derived-segment citations, and uncited bullets are dropped.
decisions.rationale: The requirement asks for speaker assignment, editable names and an explicit runtime choice, so the runtime is named: it lives in the package already selected for speech, and RESEARCH documents the configuration flags that keep it from downloading, which is also why it gets its own sandboxed service. RESEARCH establishes that v1.1.0 exposes centroid embeddings with cosine-distance helpers, that a speaker may lack a centroid, and that the declaration does not establish per-segment confidence or margin; the schema follows that boundary. Nothing in the material says how this component behaves on a three-hour meeting, and a meeting is the longest input the product produces, so the adapter carries a windowed contract that needs no capability the SDK is not already known to have, and the choice between whole-input and windowed operation is made by measurement rather than by hope. Windowing costs cross-window identity, which is measured and shown rather than hidden.

alternatives.option: Whole-input diarization with no duration contract
alternatives.tradeoff: Best possible clustering, since every segment is compared globally; leaves the memory behavior of the longest input in the product unspecified, which is the case the requirements name.

alternatives.option: Diarize a single mixed recording
alternatives.tradeoff: One file and one capture path; discards the channel signal and makes even the easiest question an inference.

alternatives.option: Treat channels as speaker identity
alternatives.tradeoff: Labels users understand immediately; wrong whenever speakers leak into the microphone or several people share a room.

alternatives.option: Apply cross-recording identity automatically above a distance threshold
alternatives.tradeoff: Less user work across a meeting series; the SDK defines no universal threshold.

alternatives.option: Ship meetings with channel labels only until a diarizer is measured
alternatives.tradeoff: Avoids shipping unmeasured attribution; drops a requested feature.

decisions.consequences: Two artifacts per meeting at native rate, roughly doubling meeting storage. Diarization weights are an explicit acquisition step, because notices for the embedder and clusterer are component-specific. Under windowed operation a speaker can appear as two clusters across a boundary until the user merges them, and the frequency of that is a measured number rather than an assumption. Attribution shown as unverified is the normal state the transcript view must explain. If measured segment-level error or correction cost exceeds its approved range, the shipped default for meetings becomes channel labels with diarization off and user-enablable, which changes a default rather than removing the feature.
decisions.reconsider_when: F5 shows whole-input operation is flat in duration, shows the API exposes per-segment evidence, or evaluation shows centroid distance is monotone with correctness allowing a derived threshold with its calibration curve.

decisions.title: History: append-only results over identified runs, full-text search, tombstones with generation tokens
decisions.choice: History lists recordings, each expandable into its processing runs and their result chains. Search is FTS5 over result text with bm25 ranking and snippets, and retained context is not indexed. Playback uses the sealed artifact. Reprocessing creates a run and inserts results; nothing is mutated, and a user-movable pointer selects the displayed run. Deletion sets a tombstone, increments a generation counter and signals cancellation; every worker carries recording id and generation from admission and commits in one transaction that aborts if the row is missing, tombstoned or at a different generation. Hard deletion happens when the last lease releases or at the next launch sweep.
decisions.rationale: A late worker response cannot recreate a deleted recording only if the existence check and the insert are the same transaction; any check-then-insert has a window. The generation counter covers delete-then-recreate at the same identifier. Organizing the list by run is what makes reprocessing through a different speech model or diarizer comparable, since each run names its inputs, its models and its code revisions.

alternatives.option: Hard delete immediately and let workers fail
alternatives.tradeoff: No tombstone bookkeeping; a constraint violation becomes the race outcome and scratch files are orphaned.

alternatives.option: Cancel workers and wait for acknowledgement before deleting
alternatives.tradeoff: No tombstone state; the user's delete blocks on a worker mid-window, and a hung worker blocks it indefinitely.

alternatives.option: Overwrite results on reprocessing
alternatives.tradeoff: One result per recording and a simpler list; comparing a new model against the old becomes impossible.

decisions.consequences: Deleted recordings hold disk until leases release, so the interface says deleting rather than claiming reclaimed space. FTS triggers must handle result deletion, covered by tests. A recording with several runs needs a detail view that makes each run's inputs and outputs obvious.
decisions.reconsider_when: Result rows dominate database size, which argues for storing older results compressed or on disk.

decisions.title: Desktop behavior: menu bar surface, software input gain, and automatic media control only through an adapter that can observe transitions
decisions.choice: An NSStatusItem shows state, current mode, recent results and settings. Microphone level is software gain on captured buffers by default, with metering and a clipping indicator; setting the input device's hardware volume is opt-in and restored only if the current value still equals the value the app set. MediaPlayerAdapter has two conformance levels. An observing adapter exposes a playback state-change stream as well as a query; a controlling-only adapter exposes a query and commands. Automatic pausing is available through either: the adapter issues a one-way pause to the identified player. Automatic resumption requires an observing adapter, and ownership exists only when the adapter observed the transition from playing to paused on the stream after the app's command. Ownership is revoked by any later observed transition, by any gap in the stream such as the player quitting or the app restarting, and by any state read that does not match the owned state. Initial observing adapters target Music and Spotify through their playback state-change notifications, each shipping as observing only after that source is confirmed in implementation and otherwise shipping as controlling-only. For a player with no adapter the app takes no automatic action: Pause media and Resume playback are explicit user actions labeled as a media-key toggle whose recipient and effect the app cannot confirm.
decisions.rationale: The specification states that automatic restoration needs an integration identifying the affected player and confirming the pause transition, and that opting in does not remove that condition. Observing the transition satisfies the confirmation clause at the moment of the pause, but ownership has to survive until the resume, and a query-only adapter cannot distinguish a pause the app owns from a play and a second pause by the user, because both leave the player paused. Splitting the contract puts automatic resume exactly where an intervening change is observable, and leaves every other player with a manual action that cannot start something the user stopped. Posting the media key automatically is excluded for the reason REVIEW_NOTES gives: a global toggle can start a paused player while an unrelated client keeps the output device active. Software gain changes no system setting, so the common case has no restore obligation.

alternatives.option: Poll the player and resume if it is still paused
alternatives.tradeoff: Works with any adapter that can read state; cannot tell an untouched pause from a play and re-pause, so it reverses a deliberate user action.

alternatives.option: Post the play-pause key automatically when the output device is running
alternatives.tradeoff: Covers every player with no adapters; the key is a toggle, so it can start playback the user stopped.

alternatives.option: Private MediaRemote framework for playback state and control
alternatives.tradeoff: Accurate per-application state without per-player adapters; an undocumented interface that can break on any OS update and complicates notarization posture.

alternatives.option: Do not touch media playback at all
alternatives.tradeoff: Nothing to get wrong; leaves background audio bleeding into recordings, which the requirement asks to address.

decisions.consequences: Automatic resume covers only players with a confirmed state-change source, so out-of-the-box coverage is narrow and grows one integration at a time, and the menu says which level a player has. Each adapter needs its own automation permission and maintenance; a player whose stream stops working degrades to controlling-only, which removes automatic resume rather than making it unsafe. The clipping indicator surfaces hardware-side clipping that software gain cannot rescue.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported system API supplies playing-application identity, pause confirmation and change notification without per-player integrations.

decisions.title: Shortcuts: distinct toggle and push-to-talk bindings, evidence-based stuck-key recovery, no duration cap
decisions.choice: A single ShortcutRegistrar owns a session-level consuming CGEventTap handling keyDown, keyUp and flagsChanged. Toggle and push-to-talk are separate bindings; a combination may be bound to at most one of them, validated at bind time. Toggle acts on keyDown. Push-to-talk starts on keyDown and finalizes on keyUp, with an optional per-binding tap-to-lock where a keyUp within 250 ms by default latches recording until the next press. Lost key-up is recovered from tap-disabled, screen lock and sleep notifications, and a 1 Hz poll of the physical key state. There is no maximum recording duration. Per-mode bindings are toggle or push-to-talk bindings with a mode attached. kCGEventTapDisabledByTimeout re-enables the tap. Without the tap, toggle falls back to Carbon RegisterEventHotKey and push-to-talk is unavailable with an explanation.
decisions.rationale: Overloading one binding with a hold discriminator leaves the first hold window undefined and makes a short press ambiguous.
