Polling the physical key state addresses the real problem, a key-up the tap never delivered, with evidence about that key, while a maximum-hold watchdog would truncate valid speech and act as the recording-duration limit the specification prohibits.

alternatives.option: One binding with a hold discriminator
alternatives.tradeoff: One combination to configure; the first hold window has undefined behavior and a dropped event changes the meaning of a press.

alternatives.option: Carbon RegisterEventHotKey only
alternatives.tradeoff: No Accessibility permission and reliable consumption; no key-up, so push-to-talk cannot exist.

alternatives.option: NSEvent global monitors only
alternatives.tradeoff: Simple API with no tap lifecycle; events cannot be consumed, so the hotkey also reaches the foreground application.

alternatives.option: A maximum hold watchdog
alternatives.tradeoff: Guarantees a stuck key eventually stops recording; truncates a genuinely long push-to-talk recording.

decisions.consequences: The app sits on the keyboard event path, so its handler must stay fast or the tap is disabled by timeout, which the re-enable path treats as a monitored condition. Users configure two shortcuts instead of one. The key-state poll runs only while a push-to-talk recording is active. Capture starting at the trigger (D-006) means a very short press still produces a short recording rather than nothing.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported API provides global hotkeys with key-up, or the poll proves unreliable for remapped or external keyboards.

decisions.title: Residency and working data under one declared budget covering every model kind and the non-model floor
decisions.choice: Budget the application at 8 GB peak on the 16 GB target, counting the app and all its services, and account for two quantities per job rather than one: model residency, meaning weights plus runtime workspace and Metal heap, and working data, meaning the ceiling the job's WorkingDataContract declares for windows, key-value cache, diarization working set and decode buffers. Slots are speech-primary, speech-preview, generation and diarization, at most one occupant each, unloaded after ten idle minutes, with admission checking the sum of both quantities across occupants. A preview-class installation qualifies for the speech-preview slot only if its declared residency is under 400 MB. Non-model ingest memory is bounded by the session and credit limits in D-004 and D-018 and is counted at a stated ceiling of 200 MB as working data. Diarization does not run concurrently with generation under the declared numbers. Activation of a pairing exceeding the budget is refused with the arithmetic shown, the refusal stating whether its numbers are measured or declared, and an override available. Once F1 and F5 descriptors exist, admission uses measured peaks and measured working-data ceilings.
decisions.rationale: The specification forbids artificial quotas and requires honest reporting of limits, which differs from ignoring the ceiling: swap on a 16 GB machine turns a latency problem into a system-wide stall. Counting only weights hides the quantity that actually grows with the work: a diarizer's embeddings and a generator's cache are not weights, and the earlier budget had no place for them, which is how a long meeting could pass admission and then exhaust memory. Declared numbers omit workspaces, so a refusal computed from them can deny a pairing that would have worked; labeling the basis and keeping the override means the policy never becomes a limit the user cannot see through.

alternatives.option: Count model weights only
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler arithmetic and fewer descriptor fields; the quantity that scales with input length sits outside the budget.

alternatives.option: Load on demand with no residency limit
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplest and fastest where memory allows; a large pairing plus a browser drives the target machine into swap.

alternatives.option: Keep selected models resident permanently
alternatives.tradeoff: Lowest per-run latency; several gigabytes held while the app idles in the menu bar.

alternatives.option: Rely on memory pressure notifications alone
alternatives.tradeoff: Adapts to real conditions; reacts after the stall has started.

decisions.consequences: First use after idle pays a model load shown as a loading state. A meeting's diarization and its notes run are sequential under the declared numbers. A job that exceeds its declared working-data ceiling is terminated with the measured figure recorded rather than the ceiling being raised silently. Until descriptors exist the budget is arithmetic that can be wrong in either direction, which the refusal text says.
decisions.reconsider_when: Measured residency and working data from F1 and F5 differ materially from declared numbers, or the app runs on machines where the ceiling does not bind.

decisions.title: Egress control enforced by the service sandbox, with no exception for any component that touches user data
decisions.choice: Inference and decoding run in services whose sandbox omits the network client entitlement, so the system denies outbound connections, and that boundary has no fallback. Downloads happen only through ModelDownloader on explicit user action, restricted to an allowlist of model hosts and writing only into staging. Runtimes receive absolute local paths through one of the three access mechanisms in D-003, are constructed with acquisition disabled, and a static check fails the build if a runtime is constructed through an initializer that can download. A user-selected external command-line decoder is shipped only if F2 shows that a child of DecodeService is confined by the service sandbox; if it is not, that adapter is not built and decoding extensions are implemented inside the service. There is no setting that runs user audio through an unconfined process. The shipped claim is that inference and decoding run in processes the system denies network access, evidenced by an in-service connection attempt that fails and by the same attempt from a spawned child; build checks, dependency-closure checks and a symbol scan corroborate that claim and do not establish it, because RESEARCH states a symbol scan cannot establish that a process lacks network access.
decisions.rationale: The specification requires that audio, transcripts and context stay on the Mac, and RESEARCH notes a diarization runtime whose default initialization may download models. The previous revision asserted the boundary and then kept the external decoder available under a disclosed trust transfer if inheritance failed, which is an exception in the one place a user's whole audio file is handed to a third-party binary. Consent does not convert a hard requirement into a preference, and the design has an alternative that satisfies both the requirement and the specification's ask for an extension mechanism, so the exception is removed rather than disclosed.

alternatives.option: Keep the external decoder with a disclosed trust transfer
alternatives.tradeoff: Any format the user can find a binary for works immediately; the process handling their audio is unconstrained, which the local-only requirement does not permit at any opt-in level.

alternatives.option: Unsandboxed service with a narrowed claim when loading fails
alternatives.tradeoff: Any runtime can be used; the offline property during normal use rests on evidence RESEARCH says cannot establish it.

alternatives.option: Allow runtimes to fetch missing models
alternatives.tradeoff: Better first run with no model manager; makes network access a side effect of loading a model.

alternatives.option: Ship no downloader and require manual placement
alternatives.tradeoff: Strongest guarantee and least code; makes first run considerably harder and pushes users toward downloading models through less careful means.

decisions.consequences: Entitlement sets are part of the signed product and a missing one fails closed. A runtime that cannot load inside the boundary is not shipped for that model kind. If F2 shows children are not confined, adding a format becomes development work rather than a user action, which is slower and is the accepted cost. Materialized caches live inside service containers and are covered by the same denial, since a container write is not an egress.
decisions.reconsider_when: F2 shows a required model kind has no adapter that loads inside the boundary, which is a specification question for the product owner rather than an implementation fallback.

decisions.title: Processing runs as the provenance spine, with a dependency table that can name non-result inputs
decisions.choice: processing_runs sits between recordings and results. Every result belongs to a run, names its primary input through primary_input_result_id where its kind has one, and records every other input in result_dependencies(result_id, input_kind, input_id, role) with input_kind in {result, speaker_assignment_revision, audio_artifact}. Recognition results are chain roots carrying the speech installation; a diarization result has no primary input, carries the diarizer installation and names its audio artifacts through dependency rows; a notes result has the transcript as primary input and dependency rows for the diarization result and the assignment revision. Invariants are stated per result kind rather than as one rule. A recording may hold several recognition and several diarization results. Results are immutable after insert, enforced by a trigger.
decisions.rationale: A recording cannot have exactly one source transcript while also being re-recognizable through a different speech model, so parentage is a foreign key rather than an inference from timestamps. A single result-typed input column could not name an assignment revision, which is not a result, so notes provenance had nothing to point at. Two result kinds legitimately have no textual parent, which is why the invariant is per kind: asserting that every non-recognition result has a primary input would fail on a correct diarization result or push an implementation to invent a parent for it.

alternatives.option: Keep one transcript per recording and forbid re-recognition
alternatives.tradeoff: The simplest graph; removes reprocessing through another speech model.

alternatives.option: Single result-typed parent, other inputs only in the manifest
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer rows; provenance queries cannot join on the second input, so History cannot show which assignment revision a note used without parsing manifests.

alternatives.option: Fixed nullable columns for transcript, diarization and assignment inputs
alternatives.tradeoff: Cheaper joins; a new result kind with a different dependency needs a migration and another column.

alternatives.option: Attach model ids to results and infer parentage by timestamp
alternatives.tradeoff: No new table; parentage becomes a guess that breaks whenever two runs overlap.

decisions.consequences: More joins in History queries and a detail view that presents runs with their inputs. The invariant suite carries one case per result kind, which is longer than one rule and is the only form that is satisfiable. The FTS index carries results from every run, so search can return two recognitions of the same audio, which the result rows disambiguate.
decisions.reconsider_when: Users never re-recognize or re-diarize, which would make the run table pure overhead, though the same structure is what makes translations and notes attributable.

decisions.title: Crash-safe capture through an fsynced chunk journal with a stated commit order and an idempotent finalization
decisions.choice: Capture writes fixed-period chunks, two seconds by default, of headerless native-rate PCM, each written to a part file, fsynced, renamed, with the directory fsynced. The sealer cycle per chunk is: encode; append packet bytes to the CAF data chunk; fsync the CAF file; append a data record and fsync it; delete covered journal chunks and fsync the directory. A data record carries magic, kind, record and chunk sequence, first packet index, packet count, frames per packet, byte offset and length, per-packet byte sizes as varints, and a CRC32. Finalization commits sealing: encode and commit every remaining chunk first, then append the pakt chunk and fsync, then patch the data chunk size and fsync, then hash and append a seal record naming the last data record, the pakt offset, the file length and the SHA-256, and fsync, then commit the rows. Recovery accepts the durable prefix by CRC and byte range; if it ends in a matching seal record the artifact is finalized, otherwise recovery truncates to the end of the last accepted data record, commits surviving journal chunks through the ordinary cycle, and runs finalization again.
decisions.rationale: Encoded bytes are fsynced before the record that names them, so recovery never builds a table over data that never reached disk, and per-packet sizes are present because an ALAC packet table cannot be reconstructed from a count and an offset. Ordering surviving chunks before the table, and making the seal record the commit point, gives a sequence that converges when repeated: any partially written table or patch is removed by truncating to the accepted prefix, and every step derives from records the application wrote and fsynced.

alternatives.option: Rebuild the table and then append surviving chunks
alternatives.tradeoff: One pass over the index; the finalized table does not describe the appended packets.

alternatives.option: Treat the presence of a pakt chunk as the commit signal
alternatives.tradeoff: No extra record; a torn pakt write is indistinguishable from a complete one.

alternatives.option: Write the container directly and rely on it being recoverable
alternatives.tradeoff: No journal, no sealer, no extra fsyncs; recovery rests on an untested property of a format that stores its table at the end.

alternatives.option: Keep raw PCM as the only durable form until the run completes
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplest recovery; transient storage equals the full raw recording.

decisions.consequences: Two fsyncs per chunk period per stream, plus three in finalization, and a recovery path that must stay idempotent under repeated crashes, which F3 tests directly. Roughly a 30-second window of journal files sits alongside the artifact during long captures, bounded by the sealer rule in D-004. If F3 shows reconstruction can be invalid, the structural fallback is to retain chunks until the finalized artifact decodes and hashes; reducing the sealed meeting sample rate is a user setting rather than a durability fallback, because it replaces the native-rate artifact irreversibly and the data lifecycle records that on the artifact.
decisions.reconsider_when: F3 shows a loss bound or a reconstruction failure the product cannot live with, or a container format with an incrementally durable index removes the need for a separate journal.

decisions.title: A state-indexed recovery contract with an explicit durability ordering rule
decisions.choice: Every non-terminal run state has an authoritative recovery transition, listed in the data lifecycle and covering arming, capturing, sealing, recognizing, diarizing, refining, rewriting, noting and delivering, plus the case of a completed meeting with no notes run. Before the sealing commit, ownership and disposition live in the session directory's fsynced manifest, and recovery honors that disposition. The ordering rule is written down: a durable record of intent precedes an externally visible irreversible effect, while a locally idempotent effect is followed by its commit. Recovery may complete deterministic stages such as refining and finalization, and never resumes generation, diarization or delivery without user action.
decisions.rationale: A recovery sweep that covers only some states leaves the rest to whichever test author reaches them first, which is the deferral the specification prohibits. Naming the ordering rule makes new stages easy to place correctly. Recording pre-commit disposition in the manifest is what makes a cancellation issued before the History row exists survive a crash, including one that arrives while the seal is still running.

alternatives.option: Discard any run in flight at a crash
alternatives.tradeoff: One rule and no partial state; throws away a completed recognition because the app crashed during a rewrite.

alternatives.option: Resume every in-flight run automatically
alternatives.tradeoff: Least user friction; re-runs generation the user may no longer want and risks re-delivering into whatever is now focused.

alternatives.option: Ask the user at launch what to do with each interrupted run
alternatives.tradeoff: No wrong default; a dialog at every launch after a crash invites blind dismissal.

decisions.consequences: Recovery does deterministic work automatically and stops at anything that consumes a model or touches another application, so a crashed meeting leaves a Generate action rather than a note. Behavior tables must cover every state, and the crash-injection suite asserts against them.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new stage appears whose effects are neither externally visible nor idempotent, which would need a rule of its own.

decisions.title: Permissions as a capability-by-state matrix
decisions.choice: A matrix over capability, run state and active adapter replaces any single revocation outcome. Losing microphone or an active system-audio stream terminates capture; losing Accessibility affects probing, insertion, readback, target revalidation and shortcut consumption and not recognition; losing Input Monitoring affects shortcuts; losing browser automation affects URL predicates; losing player automation removes that player's adapter and drops it to the manual actions in D-025; losing Screen Recording ends screen context and system-audio capture while leaving microphone capture running. Denial at launch, revocation during work and restoration each have a defined effect, and restoration is reported once.
decisions.rationale: Mapping every revocation to a capture failure would end a valid recording because the user changed a delivery permission during recognition, and would report a lost shortcut permission as an audio failure. Capabilities serve different stages, so their loss belongs at those stages.

alternatives.option: One global failure state
alternatives.tradeoff: Simple to implement and explain; stops work that is still valid and misreports the cause.

alternatives.option: Ignore revocation until the capability is next used
alternatives.tradeoff: No mid-run interruption; the user gets a confusing failure later with no connection to the change they made.

decisions.consequences: The matrix is longer than a rule, is directly testable, and becomes part of the approved behavior tables. Each capability needs a probe and a change notification path. Losing Accessibility mid-delivery makes revalidation impossible, so the attempt holds rather than posting blind.
decisions.reconsider_when: A capability appears whose loss affects several stages differently enough that the matrix needs a third dimension beyond adapter identity.

decisions.title: One artifact lease protocol after commit, session-directory ownership before it, reclamation by holder liveness
decisions.choice: A leases table records holder process id, holder process start time, connection identifier, artifact, acquisition time and heartbeat. Acquiring a lease requires the recording row to exist, be untombstoned and match the expected generation. Workers, the audio player, exports, retention policies and materialized-cache deletion acquire leases. A lease is reclaimable only when its holder is provably gone, meaning the process no longer exists or its start time differs, or its XPC connection has been invalidated; the heartbeat is displayed as progress and never on its own authorizes reclamation. Retention skips recordings with a live lease and retries on the next pass. Before the sealing commit no row exists, so ownership is the session directory, held by one RunActor, with cancellation and deletion expressed as a disposition in the fsynced manifest. Discarding audio is a distinct audio_discarded state that disables playback, re-recognition and re-diarization while leaving text reprocessing available.
decisions.rationale: One protocol for every consumer removes a class of race rather than one instance. Defining staleness by holder liveness rather than by a heartbeat interval keeps a suspended app or a worker stalled on a slow disk from having its artifact deleted underneath it. Naming the session directory as the pre-commit unit of ownership closes the gap where the protocol presupposed a row that capture does not create until sealing.

alternatives.option: Reclaim leases after a heartbeat timeout
alternatives.tradeoff: Recovers from any stall without inspecting processes; deletes an artifact a live but delayed holder is still using.

alternatives.option: Create a placeholder recording row at arming
alternatives.tradeoff: One ownership mechanism throughout; History gains rows for recordings that may never exist.

alternatives.option: Retention as immediate deletion with best-effort cancellation
alternatives.tradeoff: Policies always run on schedule; a race with an admitted job produces a timing-dependent outcome.

alternatives.option: Reference counting in memory only
alternatives.tradeoff: Cheaper than a table; counts vanish on a crash, so recovery cannot tell which artifacts were in use.

decisions.consequences: Every consumer of a committed artifact acquires a lease, including playback and cache deletion. Pre-commit work has a different ownership mechanism, so recovery has two paths to implement and test. A lease held by a process that is alive but wedged blocks retention until the user or the hang detector terminates it, which is reported rather than forced.
decisions.reconsider_when: Lease contention delays retention long enough to matter, which would argue for pausing playback and preempting batch work in place of deferring.

decisions.title: Measurements precede the boundaries they can invalidate, with approved ranges, basis and actions
decisions.choice: Five evidence gates run before the boundaries that depend on them: F1 runtime harness including its comparison and preview arms, F2 service isolation and decoder inheritance, F3 capture durability and sealer behavior, F4 insertion, error classification and pasteboard matrix, F5 diarizer inventory and duration behavior. Each gate's range, the basis of that range and the action attached to a failure are recorded in verification and approved under D-035 before the gate runs. F2's child-confinement result is a shipping condition for the external decoder adapter rather than a parameter. These gates govern shipped defaults; none gates a compatible model a user imports. Task-level phases are produced after design acceptance.
decisions.rationale: Several decisions depend on properties nothing has measured, and scheduling those after the ports and schema that depend on them would let a negative result invalidate work already built on it. Recording a range with its basis and its action is what makes a result decide something. Two gates now carry outputs that are not pass or fail but shipped data, F4's error class and profiles and F5's inventory, which is stated so nobody reads their absence as a failure.

alternatives.option: Start the skeleton immediately and measure later
alternatives.tradeoff: Visible progress sooner; a negative F1, F3 or F5 result forces rework of the ingest port, the scheduler, the capture writer or the meeting schema.

alternatives.option: Run the gates and decide acceptance after seeing the numbers
alternatives.tradeoff: Avoids arguing about thresholds in advance; invites fitting the threshold to the result.

alternatives.option: Record ranges without their basis
alternatives.tradeoff: Less text; the owner approving them cannot tell a derived criterion from an invented one.

alternatives.option: Treat the unknowns as risks accepted at implementation time
alternatives.tradeoff: No gates to schedule; hands behavioral decisions to whichever task hits them.

decisions.consequences: Some work produces evidence rather than shippable behavior, including a measurement-only comparison harness that is not part of the product. Gate outputs feed D-001, D-004, D-009, D-011, D-018, D-020, D-023, D-027, D-028, D-030, D-040 and D-042, so those decisions carry conservative defaults until the evidence lands. Approving ranges before the work adds a decision point to the schedule.
decisions.reconsider_when: A gate's fallback proves acceptable enough that the measurement is not worth its cost, which is a judgment to record instead of assume.

decisions.title: Named approval authority, specification traceability, and approved ranges with recorded basis
decisions.choice: Expected behavior lives in docs/behavior/ tables whose rows each cite a SPEC.md clause or are marked derived. The normative approver is the user as product owner, or a delegate named in docs/behavior/OWNERS. The same approver signs each gate's range, its recorded basis and its failure action before that gate runs, the rubric scoring rules for the mode corpus and the translation set before scoring, and the pre-effect error class and each delivery profile before either can license a fallthrough. Approval of a table gates writing tests against it; tests reference row identifiers; changing an approved row requires re-approval recorded in git history. Independent authorship is a hygiene rule and carries no authority.
decisions.rationale: A passing test proves only that the code met its assertions, so the assertions need an owner who can say they are the intended product behavior. Ranges are part of what gets approved because they decide which runtime and which defaults ship, and each carries its basis so the approver can distinguish a criterion derived from a design parameter from a product target with nothing behind it. The delivery error class and profiles join that list because they are the two pieces of shipped data that can license a second write into another application's document.

alternatives.option: Peer review by any team member
alternatives.tradeoff: Cheap and fast; two people can share the same misreading with nobody empowered to settle it.

alternatives.option: Approve behavior tables but leave measurement thresholds to engineering
alternatives.tradeoff: Less product-owner time; the thresholds deciding which defaults ship would have no product authority behind them.

alternatives.option: Treat SPEC.md as the only source and skip behavior tables
alternatives.tradeoff: No second artifact to maintain; the specification does not enumerate state and event pairs, so implementers fill the gaps silently.

alternatives.option: Derive expectations from the implementation and review the diff
alternatives.tradeoff: Least documentation work; makes the code its own specification.

decisions.consequences: Capability areas cannot be accepted until their tables are approved, gates cannot run until their ranges are, and delivery fallthrough data cannot ship unapproved, which puts the product owner on the critical path in three places. Derived rows and unbased ranges are visible as categories, so the volume of behavior and of thresholds with no specification or measurement basis stays measurable.
decisions.reconsider_when: Approval becomes the dominant delay, which would argue for pre-approved templates for mechanical tables instead of removing the gate.

decisions.title: Distribution: direct Developer ID distribution, ad hoc signing for local builds
decisions.choice: The application ships outside the Mac App Store, notarized under a Developer ID certificate with the hardened runtime, as an unsandboxed shell containing sandboxed XPC services. Local development builds may be ad hoc signed. App Store submission is not planned.
decisions.rationale: This is settled here rather than left as a blocking question because the specification decides it in substance: it asks for direct distribution for this worked example, and it requires a consuming session-level event tap with key-up for push-to-talk (D-026) and setting selected text in another application's accessibility element (D-009), neither of which is available to a sandboxed App Store build.

alternatives.option: Mac App Store distribution
alternatives.tradeoff: System-managed updates and a familiar install path; the sandbox removes push-to-talk and accessibility insertion as specified, so those requirements would have to be rewritten.

alternatives.option: Unsigned distribution
alternatives.tradeoff: No certificate cost; Gatekeeper blocks casual installation and every TCC grant becomes fragile.

alternatives.option: Both an App Store build and a direct build
alternatives.tradeoff: Reach plus capability; two feature sets, two permission models and two test matrices for one application.

decisions.consequences: Updates need their own mechanism, and the project carries certificate management and a notarization step in release packaging. Ad hoc signed local builds have an unstable code identity, so TCC grants for Accessibility, Input Monitoring, Screen Recording and Automation are re-requested after rebuilds; developers keep a stably signed build for permission-dependent work, documented rather than discovered. The entitlement sets in D-003 and D-028 are available because the build is not App Store sandboxed.
decisions.reconsider_when: A product decision requires App Store presence, which would require revising the Text delivery and Recording controls requirements first.

decisions.title: Notes as a separate run pinning content-addressed speaker assignments over versioned derived segments
decisions.choice: A diarization result is immutable and holds source segments, and assignment revision 1 commits with it. Everything the user can edit lives in the revision chain: speaker_assignment_revisions names its diarization result and is content-addressed; derived_segments(revision_id, id, source_segment_id, start_ms, end_ms) is the segment set that revision presents, one-to-one with source segments in revision 1 and subdivided when the user splits; speaker_assignments maps derived segments to identities. Identity display names are append-only. Notes are generated by a notes run created after those inputs commit, whose manifest pins the transcript result, the diarization result, the assignment revision and the identity-name set hash, with the first three also in result_dependencies, and whose bullets cite derived segment ranges resolved through the pinned revision. History compares pinned identifiers against current state and reports drift with a regenerate action.
decisions.rationale: Notes are the artifact whose meaning depends on user-editable data, so the snapshot rule that D-006 applies to mode settings extends to assignments, splits and names. Making notes a run that starts after its inputs commit is what makes the pin real. Splitting needed its own representation: the previous schema mapped source segment identifiers to identities, so a split had nowhere to live while the interface offered it, and a note citing a segment range could not be resolved against a boundary the user had changed. Derived segments keep the diarization result immutable while making the presented segmentation a versioned property of the revision.

alternatives.option: Allow splitting by mutating segments on the diarization result
alternatives.tradeoff: One segment table; the model output stops being immutable, and every note citing a segment range becomes unresolvable against its own provenance.

alternatives.option: Offer renaming and reassignment only, with no splitting
alternatives.tradeoff: The simplest schema; a diarizer that merges two speakers into one segment leaves the user no correction, which is exactly the case manual assignment exists for.

alternatives.option: Noting as a stage of the meeting run with a manifest extension
alternatives.tradeoff: One run per meeting; the manifest stops being a single fsynced snapshot and recovery must reason about which extension was durable.

alternatives.option: Regenerate notes automatically when assignments change
alternatives.tradeoff: Notes always current; silently replaces text the user may have relied on and spends model time on every rename.

decisions.consequences: A meeting produces at least two runs and the detail view groups them. Every speaker edit writes a revision, and the rows are small and are deleted with the recording. A crash between the diarization commit and the notes run leaves a Generate action. Assignment revisions must be reconciled when a new diarization run produces different boundaries, which carries assigned_by_user states forward where derived segments overlap in time and marks the rest unattributed.
decisions.reconsider_when: F5 shows segment identifiers are not stable enough across runs for overlap-based carry-forward, which would need a time-range mapping as the only mechanism.

decisions.title: Model installation lifecycle states bound storage when a runtime is replaced
decisions.choice: model_installations carries a lifecycle state in {installed, archived, orphaned_runtime, missing}. Archiving releases the weight assets and every materialized copy while retaining the row, the manifest and per-asset hashes, declared capabilities and the notices under Models/notices. History results keep referencing archived installations and render from results.params_rendered, and the detail view states that reprocessing needs the assets restored by import or download. Removing an adapter moves its installations to orphaned_runtime, which keeps blobs and caches on disk, lists them with their sizes and an archive action, and posts a launch-time notice; nothing is deleted without a user action. Garbage collection removes assets only when no installed or orphaned_runtime row references them and no lease is live. A pinned run against an archived installation is refused up front with a restore offer.
decisions.rationale: Reference counting alone cannot bound storage, because History results reference their installations permanently. Separating what must persist for attribution, which is small, from what must persist for execution, which is gigabytes, makes bounded storage achievable without breaking provenance. Archiving covers materialized copies as well as blobs, because a copy inside a service container is the same gigabytes under a different path and would otherwise survive the archival that claims to release them.

alternatives.option: Retain assets for any installation any result references
alternatives.tradeoff: Reprocessing always available; storage grows without bound across replacements.

alternatives.option: Archive blobs but leave materialized caches
alternatives.tradeoff: One fewer path to sweep; the released storage reappears inside a container the model manager would have to explain.

alternatives.option: Delete assets when an adapter is removed
alternatives.tradeoff: Bounded automatically; destroys reprocessing capability on a build change the user did not make.

alternatives.option: Archive automatically by age or size
alternatives.tradeoff: No user decision needed; removes reprocessing without warning.

decisions.consequences: Four installation states appear in the model manager and in History, and users must understand that an archived model is attributable but not runnable while an orphaned one is present but unusable until its adapter returns. Restoring requires the same assets by manifest hash, which the retained row makes checkable. Missing is distinguished from archived so an unexpected disappearance is reported as an error rather than a user choice.
decisions.reconsider_when: Users archive and restore the same installations repeatedly, which would argue for a compressed local cache of recent weights instead of full release.

decisions.title: Retained context as an owned artifact with a stated lifetime
decisions.choice: When a mode opts into context retention, the sample is stored as a file under Recordings/<uuid>/context/<sampleId>.txt with a retained_context row naming run, recording, source kind, representation, path, byte length and SHA-256. The file is fsynced before the transaction that inserts the row, both are removed by ordinary deletion and by retention policies, the text is not added to the FTS index, and migrations own the table like any other. Without the opt-in only the digest row exists.
decisions.rationale: Promising retained context in the interface while the schema listed digests only would leave the owner, the deletion rule and the migration path to whichever implementation task first stored a string, which is the deferral the specification prohibits for persistent data. Files rather than columns because screen recognition output can be large and because deletion then rides on the same directory removal as audio. Excluding it from the search index keeps History results about the user's own speech.

alternatives.option: Store retained context as a column on the run
alternatives.tradeoff: One fewer file kind; large samples inflate the database and its backup and migration times.

alternatives.option: Index retained context in FTS
alternatives.tradeoff: Search finds the surrounding material; searches return hits in text the user never spoke or wrote.

alternatives.option: Do not retain context at all
alternatives.tradeoff: Least storage and the simplest privacy story; reprocessing an old recording cannot reproduce its original result even when the user wants that.

alternatives.option: Encrypt retained context separately
alternatives.tradeoff: Stronger at-rest protection for the most sensitive sample; inconsistent with the audio and transcripts beside it, which would give false assurance.

decisions.consequences: Retention is visible in the library size view and in the per-recording detail. A mode that retains context makes each run larger, which the mode editor states when the option is enabled. Protection is the file system's, as for the rest of the library.
decisions.reconsider_when: A threat model asks for at-rest encryption, which would apply to the library as a whole rather than to context alone.

decisions.title: Materialized model assets are store-owned artifacts with verification, accounting and deletion rules
decisions.choice: Where F2 selects materialization for a runtime, the service copies the installation's assets from passed descriptors into materialized/<setHash>/ inside its own container, verifies every asset against the installation manifest hashes, then writes and fsyncs a materialize.done marker; the app registers materialized_assets(installation_id, service_kind, container_path, byte_length, verified_at, state) only after that marker exists. A directory without a marker or failing verification is removed and re-materialized on demand. Copies are deleted on model unload after the idle timeout, on archive, on installation deletion, on adapter removal by user action, and at launch for any directory with no registered row or whose installation has neither installed nor orphaned_runtime state; deletion acquires a lease and defers while one is live. The model manager reports materialized bytes per runtime beside blob bytes, and activation checks free space for the copy.
decisions.rationale: The third access mechanism exists so that a runtime that cannot take descriptors or a path exception can still load inside the sandbox, which is what keeps the egress boundary from having an exception. Left unowned, it would reintroduce the problem D-038 exists to solve, in a location the model manager does not enumerate: a copy could survive archival, a crash mid-copy, and a runtime replacement while never appearing in any accounting. Making it a registered artifact with a completion marker gives crash recovery a signal that does not depend on comparing sizes, and putting it under the lease protocol means a job running out of that cache cannot have it deleted underneath it.

alternatives.option: Treat the copy as private service state
alternatives.tradeoff: No table, no marker and no sweep; gigabytes accumulate outside the storage bound and outside the interface that reports library size.

alternatives.option: Materialize per job and delete at job end
alternatives.tradeoff: Nothing persists between jobs; every run pays a multi-gigabyte copy, which would dominate first-token latency.

alternatives.option: Keep copies until disk pressure forces eviction
alternatives.tradeoff: Fewer copies over time; eviction under pressure is exactly when a running job needs its assets.

alternatives.option: Symlink into the blob store from the container
alternatives.tradeoff: No second copy at all; a sandboxed process following a link out of its container is still subject to the sandbox, so this is not an access mechanism, only a rename of the path exception.

decisions.consequences: A runtime needing materialization doubles its on-disk footprint, which the model manager shows and which activation checks before starting. Verification adds a full hash pass per materialization, shown as a step. The sweep runs at launch and after unload, so a crashed copy costs at most one idle period of space.
decisions.reconsider_when: F2 shows no runtime needs materialization, which retires the mechanism and its table, or a runtime gains descriptor-based loading upstream.

decisions.title: Local model import identity when provenance metadata is absent
decisions.choice: Identity always rests on the installation-manifest hash, which is computable from the files themselves. Publisher and revision are optional labels: a download takes them from the source manifest, and a local import may leave them empty, in which case the installation records provenance unknown and shows a user-editable label defaulting to Local import plus the first twelve hex digits of the hash. Per-asset licence identifiers and notices are optional in the same way: an asset with no notice is recorded as licence unknown and activates normally, and the only consequence is that ModelDownloader will never offer that asset. Nothing about missing publisher, revision, licence, notice or benchmark data affects compatibility checking, the smoke test, activation or use.
decisions.rationale: The specification requires that compatible user-supplied models work and that an absent benchmark or quality score not disable one. An identity scheme that needed publisher and revision, or an installation path that required a notice per asset, would turn missing metadata into a compatibility gate by the back door, which is the same failure in a different field. Hashing the manifest gives a complete identity from the bytes alone, so labels can be decoration. Keeping the download restriction is different in kind: the app cannot redistribute what it has no terms for, and that limits what the app offers rather than what the user may run.

alternatives.option: Require publisher and revision for identity
alternatives.tradeoff: Human-readable identity everywhere; a compatible directory of weights cannot be installed without invented metadata.

alternatives.option: Refuse activation when an asset has no notice
alternatives.tradeoff: Every installed asset has recorded terms; the user's own model becomes unusable on a paperwork condition.

alternatives.option: Synthesize a publisher from the file path
alternatives.tradeoff: Fills the field automatically; produces identity-looking values that mean nothing and that differ if the user moves the folder.

alternatives.option: Mark provenance-unknown installations as unsupported in the interface
alternatives.tradeoff: Sets expectations about help; reads as a capability limit on a model that works, which is what the specification rules out.

decisions.consequences: History can show two installations whose only distinguishing label is a hash prefix until the user renames them, so the model manager makes the label editable and shows the hash. Notices keyed by installation mean a byte-identical import beside a downloaded install carries its own terms rather than inheriting them. Provenance unknown appears in the model detail and in the result detail, as information rather than as a warning.
decisions.reconsider_when: Users import enough unlabeled models that hash prefixes dominate the interface, which would argue for prompting for a label at import rather than changing identity.

decisions.title: Every model-bound job declares a working-data contract that is constant in input duration, and every process is measured
decisions.choice: Each adapter publishes a WorkingDataContract giving the maximum bytes the job holds beyond model weights, expressed as a constant or as a function of parameters the app controls, such as window size, credit and context length, and never as a function of input duration. Speech and decoding satisfy it through credit windows. Diarization satisfies it through whole-input operation only where F5 measures peak resident size flat in duration within its ceiling, and otherwise through 10-minute analysis windows with 30-second overlap, per-window commits and centroid-based cross-window cluster matching. Generation satisfies it through context length and windowed notes. Admission counts the declared or measured ceiling alongside residency (D-027), a job exceeding its ceiling is terminated with the measured figure recorded, and the long-input protocol samples resident size in every participating process at 10 minutes, 1 hour and 3 hours, including the app, SpeechService, DiarizationService, GenerationService, DecodeService and any decoder child.
decisions.rationale: The specification says a long file must not require memory proportional to its full decoded duration, and the previous revision established that only for recognition: credit bounded what reached the recognizer, F1 measured the app and the speech service, and diarization and decoding were left to inherit a property nobody had checked. A diarizer that loads a whole waveform or accumulates embeddings, or a decoder that buffers a file before emitting anything, would each break the requirement while every credit window in the design stayed correctly bounded, because credit bounds a queue and not a producer. Making the contract a published property per adapter, and the measurement per process, puts the obligation where the memory is.

alternatives.option: Rely on credit alone
alternatives.tradeoff: One mechanism to implement; bounds queues between components and says nothing about what a component holds internally.

alternatives.option: Measure only the app and the speech service
alternatives.tradeoff: Cheaper protocol; the two processes whose duration behavior is least known are the ones not measured.

alternatives.option: Cap meeting and import duration instead
alternatives.tradeoff: Bounds memory trivially; the specification forbids artificial recording-duration limits.

alternatives.option: Window everything unconditionally
alternatives.tradeoff: One code path and a guaranteed bound; pays the cross-window identity cost even where a runtime is measurably flat and would cluster better globally.

decisions.consequences: Adapters carry an extra descriptor field that must be kept honest, and a wrong declaration surfaces as a terminated job rather than as swap. Windowed diarization can split one speaker across a boundary until the user merges, which the transcript marks and the evaluation measures. The long-input protocol is longer and needs process-level sampling harnessing rather than a single memory graph.
decisions.reconsider_when: A runtime exposes a memory contract of its own that the descriptor can carry directly, or measurements show a component whose growth is bounded but not constant, which would need a declared function rather than a ceiling.

coverage.explanation: Global toggle and push-to-talk from another application come from one session-level event tap that observes key-up and consumes the hotkey (D-026), available because of the distribution decision in D-036. Toggle and push-to-talk are separate configurable bindings validated at bind time, so a press has one meaning; per-mode bindings select a mode and start a run in one action. A lost key-up is recovered from tap-disabled and screen-lock notifications and from polling the physical key state, so there is no maximum hold and no duration cap. Capture starts at the trigger into a pre-roll ring while arming runs concurrently (D-006), so a user who speaks immediately does not lose the first word, and the residual device-start latency is measured by the leading-audio test. Without Accessibility or Input Monitoring the tap cannot run, so toggle falls back to a Carbon hotkey and push-to-talk is unavailable with an explanation (D-032). Cancellation has a defined effect at every stage a run can occupy, including sealing, diarizing and noting (D-007); cancelling during sealing returns immediately and records a durable disposition that is applied when the idempotent seal finishes or at recovery, so the escape path does not wait on encode or disk. A crash mid-run resolves through the state-indexed recovery contract, which covers the same stage set and the meeting-without-notes case (D-031).

The processed transcript is inserted at the caret or over the current selection by setting AXSelectedText; the app never sets an element's whole value, so existing field contents survive (D-009), following the distinction RESEARCH draws between an accessibility object's value and its selected text. D-008 resolves exactly one target per focus outcome and then revalidates the frontmost process, window and focused element immediately before every posted event and before the submit Return, because those events reach whatever is focused when they are posted. Duplicate delivery is prevented by making each fallthrough depend on evidence that rung can actually produce. A settability probe runs before any write, so a target that cannot take accessibility insertion reaches the pasteboard rung with nothing having touched it. After a write is issued, only error codes in an approved pre-effect class that F4 populates permit the next rung, and messaging failures and timeouts are excluded permanently, because a request the target was too busy to answer may still be applied. An unchanged readback after Command-V is never treated as rejection, since a delayed consumer can apply the paste afterwards, so synthesized typing runs only when an applicable profile's rejection signal fires, and a profile is applicable only while its recorded application and macOS versions cover the running target and its measurement has not expired. Every other outcome is a content-based confirmation or an unconfirmed stop. Optional submission posts Return after a confirmed delivery, whichever rung achieved it, and only after re-checking that the delivered text still sits where it was confirmed, so an edit or caret move between confirmation and Return suppresses it. Clipboard changes are handled by snapshotting before writing and restoring only after confirmed delivery while the change count is ours, or on the user's action; after an unconfirmed outcome the transcript stays on the clipboard and the panel says so. Permissions denied or revoked route the result to History and the clipboard through the capability matrix (D-032), and secure input suppresses synthesis. Recovery is complete because the attempt row never rests in a state without a transition: rejection is a rung outcome, the handoff between rungs is one transaction, and pending, in_progress and unconfirmed become needs_review at launch while delivered, held and failed are left alone (D-010).

A provisional live transcript comes from a pass over a sliding window and a waveform is drawn from a 10 ms RMS and peak envelope computed allocation-free on the capture thread (D-011). The compact window is a non-activating, borderless panel at status-bar level that joins all spaces, is movable by its background and never becomes key, so showing it cannot disturb the delivery target. Placement is remembered as a fraction of the display's visible frame plus the display identifier and clamped to the primary display when either is gone. Provisional text renders in a secondary style with a live label and is replaced by the final transcript with a change highlight; the provisional stream is never persisted, because it was produced over partial context and is a different artifact from the recognition result the run commits (D-006). Failures appear as a panel row with a short reason and one action. The ladder that keeps provisional text available is executable rather than nominal: an interactive run reserves the speech-primary slot and preempts batch speech work (D-004), and a preview-class installation under 400 MB has its own slot counted in the budget together with its working data (D-027). Each rung has stated criteria for first-text latency, update interval, dropped frames and final-transcript quality, the last of them a paired non-inferiority test with a defined bound and sample size rather than an appeal to measurement noise. Waveform-only is not an accepted end state; if no rung meets its criteria on the evaluation target, that is a release question for the product owner.

Four built-in modes cover ordinary dictation and task-specific output: Standard, Email, Note and Meeting notes (D-013), each carrying a structured contract rather than a prose description. Standard is limited to punctuation, capitalization, optional disfluency removal and vocabulary substitution; Email adds template salutation and sign-off, paragraph structure and register adjustment with no new factual content; Note adds list and heading structure; Meeting notes permits summarization because that is its purpose and is bounded by a citation requirement against derived segment ranges. All four declare that they do not answer questions, and what the design claims about that declaration is bounded by what its checks establish (D-012). The language-independent set always runs, covering expansion ratio, context overlap, vocabulary survival and script sanity, with orthographic question-mark detection reported as a signal. Where a validator pack exists, the language-dependent set checks interrogative survival in order, content-word recall and unsupported sentences, and an observed violation retries once and then delivers the normalized transcript while retaining the generated text marked contract_violation. Where no pack exists, the rewrite is produced and retained but the delivered text is the normalized transcript, because the check that protects the declaration is the one missing and a question-mark signal cannot establish that no question was asked; no setting overrides this. These checks are necessary conditions, not proof of fidelity, which is why the adversarial corpus and the scored rubric rule in verification decide whether a built-in ships.

Users author prompts and formatting rules, and each custom mode fills in a structured contract naming its allowed operations, whether it may answer questions, its content bound, the languages its validator supports and the representation of each context source; the editor cannot save a mode without one, because a free-form prompt gives the checker nothing to check against (D-012). Each mode selects its own local speech and language models by content identity rather than by name, and that identity covers every behavior-affecting asset (D-022) and is computable for a user-imported model with no publisher or licence metadata, so a custom mode can select a model the user built or converted themselves (D-041). Every save creates a content-addressed revision in an append-only chain, and every run pins the revision id into its manifest at start along with model installations, runtime and adapter revisions, vocabulary revision, language and validator pack set (D-006). Work already in progress reads its snapshot and never live settings, so editing a mode or updating a runtime during a recognition cannot change what the running job produces, and a saved result keeps pointing at the revision and the code revision that produced it. History names the producing revision and diffs it against the current one. Because every result also names its run and its inputs (D-029), a rewrite produced by an old revision stays attributable after the audio is recognized again under a different model. Check coverage never restricts model choice: the rewrite is always produced and retained, and what varies is which checks ran and whether it is delivered automatically.

Rules match the foreground application's bundle identifier and, where readable, the website URL, evaluated at arming with first match winning over a user-ordered list (D-014). List position is the complete precedence rule, so the answer is readable off the list from top to bottom; specificity only proposes an insertion point in the editor and flags rules an earlier rule shadows, which is why no priority field exists to be tie-broken against. When a predicate's input cannot be obtained, because browser automation is denied, the browser exposes no URL, or screen recording is off, rules needing that input do not match and evaluation continues; if nothing matches, the user's default mode applies. Permission loss is handled per capability, so losing browser automation narrows rule matching without disturbing capture or recognition (D-032). The chosen mode is latched into the run manifest, so it cannot change mid-sentence, and the effective mode plus whether it came from a rule or the fallback appears in the recording panel and the menu bar for every run, which is what keeps the current mode apparent (D-011). Which browsers expose a URL is enumerated in a dated matrix before URL rules ship, and an incomplete matrix degrades to bundle-identifier rules.

User terminology and names enter at four points with a fixed order relative to recognition and language processing (D-015). Before recognition, selected terms go into the decoder's prompt slot, bounded by the runtime's limit and chosen by mode relevance and recency; that shifts decoding probabilities and the interface says exactly that, with no claim that adding a name guarantees recognition, because the mechanism is a prompt rather than a decoding constraint (D-020). After recognition, replacements run deterministically over the recognition result with an explicit match precedence: longest match at each position, ties broken by list order, boundary-aware using ICU segmentation for the run's language, case-preserving, non-overlapping and applied once with no cascading, so two implementations cannot produce different normalized transcripts while satisfying the same prose. Where segmentation is unavailable the pipeline falls back to substring matching with a warning in the editor. Filler removal is a separate per-mode pass. After generation the table is applied once more, and vocabulary survival is a language-independent check, so it runs whether or not a pack exists (D-012); a model that normalizes an unusual proper noun back to a common word is caught and the user's spelling wins. Recognition and normalized results are both retained, so the effect of each stage is inspectable.

Three optional sources are sampled at arming in parallel against a 200 ms deadline: focused-element text, selection and window title through accessibility; one frame of the focused window through ScreenCaptureKit with Vision text recognition when opted in; and the first text item on the pasteboard, each capped (D-016). Sampling once at arming bounds cost and makes a run reproducible, and anything missing the deadline is omitted and recorded as omitted. Context is data supplied to a mode, and every source is treated the same way: all three are distilled to a capped term list before reaching the prompt, which removes instruction-shaped sentences rather than detecting them afterwards. A mode may opt a source into prose, and then automatic delivery additionally requires the language-dependent check set to be available and to pass; otherwise the normalized transcript is delivered and the generated text is held (D-012). The residual limit is stated rather than papered over: an instruction obeyed in words absent from the context is not detectable by any listed check, and what bounds the damage is that the transcript is preserved and delivery is the only automatic external effect. Retention defaults to a digest, and opting in stores an owned artifact with a row, a path and deletion rules that ride on the recording (D-039). Every transient copy has a release point on every path a run can take, including a run with no generation stage, which releases prose sources at the end of refining, and any terminal state, which releases them regardless. No inference service writes prompts or context to disk. Missing permissions leave a named operating state (D-032), and context never leaves the machine because it crosses only an XPC connection to a service the system denies network access, with no component excepted from that boundary (D-028).

Recognition language is set per mode to an explicit code or to detection using the runtime's language identification against a recorded threshold that starts at 0.5 and has its own measurement protocol; below it the run records undetermined, uses the mode's default and the panel says so (D-017). Translation into English is a separate declared operation that inserts a result naming the exact recognition or normalized result it translated, so the source transcript is preserved beside any derived text and stays identifiable after the same audio is recognized again under a different model (D-029). The three properties are evaluated by three methods and reported separately: recognition by word error rate per language, rewriting by the mode rubric, and translation by a bilingual set of 30 utterances per source language scored for adequacy, names and numbers, and added content against the retained source transcript rather than against the audio, so a recognition error is charged to recognition. Compatibility is declared per installation and checked against the per-kind runtime descriptor at activation (D-022); the interface attributes language claims to the model publisher and marks them unmeasured until an evaluation row exists. Pack coverage restricts neither which models may be used nor which languages may be recognized or translated: without a pack the model runs, the result is produced, retained and searchable, and the language-independent checks still apply. What a missing pack changes is the automatic delivery of a rewrite for a mode that declares it does not answer questions, which is a property of the mode's own declaration rather than a limit on the model (D-012).

Microphone, system audio and imported audio and video all implement one AudioSource emitting native-format frames carrying stream id, clock domain, presentation time, sequence and a discontinuity flag, with conversion to the canonical 16 kHz mono input as an explicit stage after the port (D-018). Consumers grant credit, so a seekable source stops decoding when the recognizer falls behind and a live source that overruns records a discontinuity rather than buffering without bound. The initial format matrix is what the system decoders cover: wav, aiff, caf, mp3, m4a in AAC and ALAC, mp4, m4v and mov. The extension mechanism is a DecoderProvider port with two possible implementations chosen by F2: a user-selected external command-line decoder, shipped only if a child of the decode service is confined by the service sandbox, or a decoder built into that service. There is no setting that runs a user's audio through an unconfined process, because consent cannot waive the requirement that captured audio stays on the Mac (D-028). The memory requirement is met by a contract rather than by inheritance from credit: every model-bound job declares a working-data ceiling that is constant in input duration, the decoder consumes its input as a stream, and the long-input protocol samples resident size in every participating process at 10 minutes, 1 hour and 3 hours, since credit bounds a queue and says nothing about what a producer holds (D-042). Concurrency is bounded: one live capture session at a time, and seekable ingest occupies one of a bounded number of ingest slots, while live capture writing and sealing stay exempt from admission because deferring a live source loses audio (D-004). A failed import leaves its source unchanged because the path opens it read-only, copies into the session directory and commits only after the artifact is complete; on failure the directory is removed and no row exists (D-019).

A meeting captures microphone and system audio as two artifacts whose frames carry host-time stamps, so alignment and gaps are represented by the ingest port rather than reconstructed afterwards (D-018), with a stated drift range and a tone-derived correction, and capture is crash-safe through the chunk journal and its idempotent finalization (D-030). Channel origin is recorded as a fact about capture and labeled as the microphone channel and the system audio channel; it is not presented as speaker identity (D-023). Speaker separation has an explicit runtime and an explicit home: SpeakerKit's Pyannote pipeline behind a Diarizer port in its own sandboxed DiarizationService with download disabled, an explicit model folder and explicit concurrency recorded in the manifest, with weights acquired by the user. Diarization is a run stage with a cancellation effect, a recovery transition and admission accounting, and both its model residency and its working-data ceiling count against the budget beside speech, preview and generation (D-006, D-027). Because a meeting is the longest input the product produces and nothing in the available material describes this component's behavior over hours, the adapter carries a duration contract: whole-input operation only where F5 measures it flat within its ceiling, and otherwise 10-minute analysis windows with overlap, per-window commits and centroid-based cross-window matching, whose identity cost is measured and shown rather than assumed away (D-042). Evidence is represented at the boundary the cited declaration supports: per-segment calibrated confidence is unknown, no per-segment margin is stored, and centroid distance proposes cross-recording identity for confirmation. Segments default to unverified and notes attribute only assigned segments. Assigning, merging, splitting and renaming all append revisions over versioned derived segments, so a split has a representation and a note's citations resolve against the segmentation its revision presented, and notes are a separate run created after the diarization result and revision 1 commit, pinning all of them in a manifest fsynced at that run's start and in dependency rows that can name an assignment revision (D-037, D-029). Timestamped notes cite derived segment ranges and drop uncited bullets. Diarization quality is reported with its components separated and with a segment-level measure and a correction-cost measure, and the range decides the shipped default rather than the feature's availability.

Recordings are searchable through FTS5 over result text with bm25 ranking and snippets, and playable from the sealed artifact (D-005, D-024). Each recording expands into its processing runs, and each run into a result chain rooted at that run's recognition or diarization result, so reprocessing through another model or mode inserts a new run and new results while every earlier result stays immutable and attributable (D-029). The relationship between original audio and successive results is one recording to many runs to many results, each naming its primary input where its kind has one, its other inputs by role and kind, the mode revision, the model installations and the runtime and adapter revisions that produced it; the invariants asserted over that graph are stated per result kind, because a diarization result correctly has no textual parent. A user-movable pointer selects the displayed run. Deletion while processing is active sets a tombstone, increments a generation counter and signals cancellation; every worker carries the recording id and generation from admission and commits in one transaction that aborts if the row is missing, tombstoned or at a different generation, so a late response cannot recreate a deleted recording. Deletion requested before the sealing commit is a manifest disposition, since no row exists to tombstone (D-033). Retention is not a separate mechanism: age, size and audio-discarding policies acquire the same leases, skip recordings held by a live holder, and move audio to a discarded state that disables playback, re-recognition and re-diarization while leaving text reprocessing available. A lease is reclaimed only when its holder is provably gone. Interrupted work resolves through the state-indexed recovery contract, which covers diarizing and noting (D-031), and space is reported as deleting until the last lease releases.

The model library browses and manages installed speech, preview, language and diarization models with their capabilities, sizes, per-asset licences where known and owning runtime (D-022). Identity is a hash over a manifest covering every behavior-affecting asset, including tokenizer, configuration and template, and each run additionally records the runtime and adapter revision, so a result names what produced it including the code. Because that hash is computable from the files alone, a compatible local model imports and activates with no publisher, revision, licence or benchmark metadata, labeled provenance unknown and unmeasured, and nothing about missing metadata gates compatibility; the only consequence is that the app will not offer those assets for download (D-041). Compatibility and the smoke test are per kind, so a diarizer missing its clusterer or a speech model missing its tokenizer fails at install rather than mid-run, and that test is a capability check and never a quality judgment. Installation stages, verifies, smoke-tests, then renames into an immutable content-addressed directory, after which one transaction records the installation and moves the active pointer; notices are keyed by installation rather than by content, so two installations sharing a blob keep their own terms and archiving cannot delete them. A failed download or import cannot replace a working installation. Model loading never triggers a download: runtimes receive absolute paths through one of three access mechanisms, initializers that can fetch are prohibited by a build check, acquisition is confined to an explicitly invoked downloader on a host allowlist, and all four inference services are denied the network by their sandbox with no component excepted (D-028, D-003, D-023). Replacing a runtime has bounded effect on interface and storage: runtimes are separate adapter targets and service binaries with their own descriptors and parameter schemas (D-002, D-020, D-021), old rows render from params_rendered after an adapter is removed, removing an adapter marks installations orphaned_runtime without deleting anything, and archiving releases both blobs and every materialized service-container copy while retaining identity, hashes and notices (D-038, D-040). Those copies are registered, hash-verified, lease-aware and swept, so the storage bound covers every access mechanism rather than only the shared blob store. Activation exceeding the budget, which counts model residency and declared working data for speech, preview, generation and diarization together with the non-model floor, is refused with the arithmetic shown, labeled measured or declared, and overridable (D-027).

A menu bar status item is the always-available surface showing state, effective mode, recent results and settings, complementing the recording panel (D-011, D-025). Microphone level adjustment is software gain on captured buffers by default, with metering and a clipping indicator, so the common case changes no system state and has nothing to restore; setting the input device's hardware volume is opt-in and restored only if the current value still equals what the app set, with any mismatch leaving the setting as found and saying so. Media control is confined to what the app can own over time, not only at the moment of the pause. An adapter identifies the player and issues a one-way pause to it, and automatic resumption additionally requires an adapter that exposes a playback state-change stream, because ownership must survive until the resume: a query-only adapter that finds the player paused cannot distinguish an untouched pause from a play and a second pause by the user, so such an adapter may pause and may offer manual resume and never resumes automatically. Ownership is revoked by any observed transition, any gap in the stream, and any state that does not match. For a player with no adapter the app takes no automatic action at all, because the media key is a toggle that can start a paused player while an unrelated client keeps the output device active; Pause media and Resume playback are explicit user actions labeled with that uncertainty. Competing applications and manual user edits therefore produce no automatic restoration and a note that playback or the setting was left as found. Losing automation permission for a player removes its adapter and drops that player to the manual actions (D-032). The macOS baseline and the public APIs these behaviors use are set by D-001, with anything newer behind an availability check and a defined fallback.

open_questions.question: Which of the three access mechanisms does each runtime need to load its models inside a sandboxed service with the network entitlement withheld, and is a child process spawned by DecodeService confined by that service's sandbox?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F2, before the entitlement set, the access path and the decoder extension mechanism are frozen. Load each model kind by descriptor passing, by a read-only path exception scoped to Models/blobs, and by materialization inside the service container with hash verification; attempt outbound connections and a write outside the job scratch and materialized directories and assert both fail; repeat from a spawned child. The boundary is fixed either way. If a runtime loads under none of the mechanisms, the alternative adapter behind the same port is used. If the spawned child is not confined, the external decoder adapter is not built and decoding extensions are implemented inside the service, which is slower per format and keeps the requirement intact. Only the case where a required model kind has no adapter that loads inside the boundary reaches the product owner, as a specification question.

open_questions.question: Which accessibility error codes, if any, are returned only before the target applied the write, so that falling through to the pasteboard rung cannot duplicate text?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F4 populates the approved pre-effect class from observed behavior per code, per target and per version, and the class ships empty until it does. Messaging failures and timeouts are excluded permanently by rule, since a request the target was too busy to answer may still be applied. The ladder does not wait on the answer, because the settability probe already routes targets that cannot take accessibility insertion, and an unclassified error simply ends the attempt as unconfirmed with the transcript on the pasteboard and a Deliver again action. A permanently empty class costs one click in the rare case where a write failed after the probe was optimistic.

open_questions.question: How does the shipping speech runtime behave on long input and under cancellation, and does it meet the accuracy, latency and memory ranges for the default pairing?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F1, with ranges, bases, aggregation rules and failure actions approved under D-035 before it runs. F1 builds a measurement-only whisper.cpp harness alongside the shipping adapter so the retention comparison is executable, with the comparator checkpoint and quantization rule fixed in advance and a switch to an absolute margin where the comparator's word error rate is small enough that a relative one is meaningless. It also measures cancellation latency, checkpoint equivalence and the preview arm under a paired non-inferiority test. Failure of a range promotes the harness to a shipping adapter or changes the default model size, both of which satisfy the same requirement.

open_questions.question: How much captured audio is lost when the writer is killed at an arbitrary offset, does finalization survive a crash at every one of its write boundaries, and does the sealer hold its backlog bound under contention?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F3, before recovery expectations for capturing and sealing are approved. Kill the writer at randomized offsets across chunk boundaries, at both per-chunk fsync points and at every finalization write, and kill again during recovery, asserting a maximum lost interval of at most 4 seconds, a decodable artifact whose packet count matches the durable prefix, and convergence of repeated recovery. Separately measure the backlog with a concurrent import and a loaded CPU. If the interval is exceeded, shorten the chunk period; if reconstruction is ever invalid, retain journal chunks until the finalized artifact decodes and hashes; if the backlog exceeds its bound, reduce ingest slots and raise encode priority, leaving a reduced meeting sample rate as a user setting rather than an automatic response, because it replaces the native-rate artifact irreversibly.

open_questions.question: Which targets support selected-text insertion with a preserved field, allow the confirmation predicate to be evaluated, and expose a rejection signal that would justify a synthesized-typing profile entry, and for which application and system versions?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F4, before delivery profiles ship. Prototype the probe, rung 1 and rung 2 with readback in the applications listed under verification, recording content survival, predicate evaluability, per-error-code effects, any rejection signal, pasteboard read timing and snapshot cost by content type, with the application and macOS versions recorded in every cell, because those versions scope the resulting profiles and their expiry. The ladder does not wait on the table: with no applicable profile, synthesized typing is unreachable and an uncertain outcome is unconfirmed with the transcript left on the pasteboard.

open_questions.question: Which fields does the pinned SpeakerKit version expose, does it accept incremental input, and does DiarizationService hold memory proportional to meeting duration?
open_questions.resolution: Gate F5, a thin adapter experiment before the meeting schema, the diarization working-data contract and the residency numbers freeze. RESEARCH establishes centroid embeddings with cosine-distance helpers and establishes that per-segment confidence and margin are not exposed, so the schema already stores unknown for those; F5 confirms the field list at the pinned version, measures peak resident size at 10 minutes, 1 hour and 3 hours, and supplies the numbers admission needs.
